Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

providers.name: Cloover
providers.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.

providers.name: BWX Technologies
providers.description: BWX Technologies is a manufacturer of nuclear components and provider of nuclear services to the U.S. government and commercial customers worldwide. The company delivers innovative nuclear solutions across naval propulsion, small modular reactors, nuclear fuel, medical isotopes, and complex site operations.

providers.name: Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board
providers.description: The Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board (DNFSB) is an independent organization within the executive branch of the United States Government chartered to provide recommendations and advice to the President and the Secretary of Energy on public health and safety issues at Department of Energy defense nuclear facilities. The DNFSB publishes recommendations, letters, technical reports, weekly site-representative reports, and rulemaking notices through its public website and FOIA reading room. The agency does not publish a developer-oriented API; programmatic users rely on document downloads, RSS feeds, and Federal Register integrations.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Rondo Energy
providers.description: Rondo Energy is an Alameda, California industrial decarbonization company led by CEO John O'Donnell that builds the Rondo Heat Battery (RHB), a thermal energy storage system that converts intermittent wind and solar electricity into heat stored in thousands of tons of refractory brick at temperatures up to 1,500C and returns it as continuous steam, thermal oil, superheated air, or combined heat and power at rated outputs from 2MWth to over 100MWth. The RHB is sold as a drop-in replacement for a fossil-fuel boiler, via capital purchase, lease, or heat purchase agreement, into cement, food and beverage, chemicals, fuels and ethanol, textiles, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceuticals, and direct air capture. Rondo operates the world's largest industrial heat battery and has announced a 90GWh factory plan with Siam Cement Group, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Catalyst, Energy Impact Partners, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Rio Tinto, SABIC, Aramco Ventures, and the European Investment Bank. Rondo sells hardware and delivered heat, not software: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Nexamp
providers.description: Nexamp is a Boston-based clean energy company, founded in 2007 by two U.S. Army veterans, that develops, builds, owns and operates distributed solar generation and battery storage across the United States and is one of the country's largest fully integrated community solar providers. The company runs end-to-end: project development and acquisition, engineering and design, construction, asset operations, and subscriber management for residential and commercial community solar customers, alongside power purchase agreements, land leasing for solar farm hosts, energy storage, and standalone development and asset-management services. Customer-facing software is delivered through the community.nexamp.com subscriber portal and the portal.nexamp.com Decarbonization Platform. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass Nexamp publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract; the api.nexamp.com host that exists is gated behind Microsoft Entra ID and is not publicly documented.

providers.name: Amperecloud
providers.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Haven Energy
providers.description: Haven Energy is an Austin, Texas based residential clean-energy company that sells, finances, installs and operates home battery storage and solar systems, and then aggregates those systems into one of the largest virtual power plant (VPP) networks in the United States. Homeowners get an instant online quote, a fixed monthly payment over a ten-year term, end-to-end permitting and certified installation through Haven's Channel Partner network of local electricians, and ongoing remote monitoring. Haven then enrolls the installed batteries into utility and grid programs - California SGIP, PG&E, and Massachusetts ConnectedSolutions among them - so customers can monetize grid participation while utilities and community choice aggregators gain flexible local capacity. Founded in 2022 by Jeff Chapin, Philip Krim and Vinnie Campos, the company raised a $40M Series B in December 2025 led by Giant Ventures. Haven operates as a direct-to-consumer and utility-partner business; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Last Energy
providers.description: Last Energy is an American developer and operator of micro-modular nuclear power plants, founded in 2019 in Washington, D.C. by Bret Kugelmass as a commercial spinout of the Energy Impact Center. Its flagship PWR-20 is a 20 MWe pressurized water reactor assembled from a few dozen factory-made, steel-encased modules that ship to site and are installed rather than constructed in place. Last Energy sells power rather than reactors: it designs, finances, owns and operates plants under long-term power purchase agreements for energy-intensive customers including data centers, metals, chemicals, cement, pulp and paper, and food and beverage. The company has announced projects in Texas, South Wales, Poland and Romania, entered nuclear site licensing in the United Kingdom, partnered with Texas A&M and DP World, and raised roughly $164M across a $40M Series B and a $100M Series C. Last Energy publishes a marketing site and a gated customer/whitepaper portal, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Vistra Corp
providers.description: Vistra Corp (NYSE: VST) is an Irving, Texas integrated retail electricity and power generation company and the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating roughly 41,000-44,000 MW of natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery storage capacity alongside a retail business serving nearly 5 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across 16 states and the District of Columbia through TXU Energy, Dynegy, Ambit Energy, Energy Harbor, Homefield Energy and U.S. Gas & Electric. Its home market is the United States, where it sits on both sides of the competitive value chain, a merchant generator selling into ERCOT, PJM, ISO-NE, NYISO, MISO and CAISO, and a retail electricity provider (REP) reselling that power to end customers. Its API posture is honestly none. No developer portal, no API subdomain and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found: developer., developers., docs., api. and data. on vistracorp.com do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /data, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return 404; and TXU Energy's 758-URL sitemap contains no developer or API page. The United States has no consumer energy data mandate. Green Button is an NAESB/NIST ESPI standard adopted voluntarily, and TXU Energy appears on the US Department of Energy's list of "Utilities Committed to Implementing Green Button", a 2012-era commitment list and not evidence of a live endpoint. The only customer-data surface found is Download-My-Data-style export behind the TXU Energy MyAccount login, whose interval readings are themselves sourced from Smart Meter Texas, the shared ERCOT meter-data platform operated by the transmission and distribution utilities (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) rather than by Vistra. Because Vistra is a retailer and generator and not a wires company, the third-party interval-data API in its home Texas market belongs to Smart Meter Texas and not to Vistra. Vistra likewise publishes no open market or grid data of its own; ERCOT, the other ISOs/RTOs and the EIA publish the market data about Vistra's fleet. Both sides are therefore closed at the company boundary. Not to be confused with Vistra Limited (vistra.com), the unrelated corporate-services and fund-administration firm that does run a real API developer portal at devportal.vistra.com.

providers.name: UGI Corporation
providers.description: UGI Corporation is a Fortune 500 international energy distribution and services company headquartered in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania. UGI distributes natural gas, liquid propane, and electricity primarily through four business segments: UGI Utilities (natural gas and electric distribution in Pennsylvania), AmeriGas Propane (largest US propane marketer), Midstream and Marketing, and UGI International (European energy distribution). No public developer API has been identified; the company primarily uses EDI and utility industry standards for B2B data exchange.

providers.name: Beyond Limits
providers.description: Beyond Limits (trading as BeyondAI) is an enterprise and industrial artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Glendale, California, built on cognitive and neuro-symbolic AI technology licensed from Caltech and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Its Hybrid AI Platform combines machine learning, generative AI and rule-based symbolic reasoning so that industrial operators get explainable, auditable recommendations instead of black-box predictions. Products include the Hybrid AI Platform (with Data, ML Ops/PRE, KB Ops and a low-code API available under a development license), Operations Advisor, Beyond Search generative AI, AI in a Box on-premises infrastructure, and DocLink document process automation from its Altec subsidiary. The company sells into energy and LNG, oil and gas, refining, petrochemicals, utilities, mining, manufacturing, aerospace and critical infrastructure. Beyond Limits publishes no public developer portal, API reference or self-service sign-up; platform API access is granted to licensed customers, so there is no publicly discoverable machine-readable contract for this provider.

providers.name: Neara
providers.description: Neara is a physics-enabled digital twin platform for electric utilities and network operators. It builds a single, physics-accurate 3D model of a utility's entire network from LiDAR, GIS, and imagery, then runs engineering-grade simulations across vegetation management, wildfire and flood mitigation, severe-weather response, clearance and conductor-clash analysis, pole utilization and FEA, asset inspection and lifecycle management, and transmission and distribution network design. Utilities use Neara to plan, harden, and operate their grids at scale — forecasting and backcasting resilience, prioritizing risk, and optimizing capital spend across millions of assets. Founded in Australia, Neara operates regionally across ANZ, the USA, and Europe.

providers.name: Arbor
providers.description: Arbor is a consumer energy savings service operating in deregulated electricity markets across 13 states in the U.S. Northeast, Midwest, and Texas. The Arbor app analyzes a household's current electricity supply rate, matches the customer with vetted alternative suppliers, and automatically switches them to a lower-cost plan when one becomes available, all without changing the utility provider, interrupting service, or charging the customer. Arbor earns revenue through referral fees from energy suppliers rather than from consumers. Founded in 2022 by Andrew Meyer (previously co-founder of Swell Energy), Arbor is backed by First Round Capital, Obvious Ventures, Spring Tide Capital, and Blisce. Arbor is a consumer-facing application and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Fuse
providers.description: Fuse Energy is a UK retail energy supplier providing gas and electricity to homes and businesses, alongside EV charging, solar and battery storage tracking with grid export, and smart home energy management. The company emphasises savings against the UK price cap, a fast (~3 minute) online sign-up, automated supplier switching, and 24/7 customer support including an AI assistant called "Plugs". Fuse was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer/business energy web and mobile experience and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (Fuse Energy Supply Limited) is a UK-based residential and business energy supplier providing gas and electricity on variable, fixed, and multi-rate tariffs, alongside EV charging, solar and battery export tracking, multi-property account management, and an in-app AI energy assistant called Plugs. The company positions itself around beating the UK energy price cap, sign-up in under three minutes, and 24-hour customer support. It operates a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile app experience and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Vectren (CenterPoint Energy)
providers.description: Vectren Corporation was a Fortune 1000 energy holding company headquartered in Evansville (Newburgh), Indiana providing regulated natural gas and electric distribution services to customers in Indiana and Ohio, along with non-regulated infrastructure services and energy efficiency programs. Vectren merged with CenterPoint Energy on February 1, 2019 in a $6 billion transaction, becoming part of the combined company which serves over 7 million metered customers across Arkansas, Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Ohio, Oklahoma, and Texas. Vectren customer-facing portals continue to operate at vectren.com redirecting to CenterPoint Energy services.

providers.name: FYLD
providers.description: FYLD is an AI-native frontline intelligence platform for the global critical-infrastructure sector, turning field-operations data into real-time, structured intelligence for utilities, energy, and heavy-civils operators. Its products include the FYLD Platform for work execution, FYLD Control Room for remote supervision, and FYLD ShowMe for customer self-service reporting, serving managers, fieldworkers, contractors, and civil engineers via web and mobile (iOS and Android) apps. FYLD is a Partech portfolio company. As of this profile FYLD publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; integration is delivered through partnerships such as Procore, and this record captures its public identity, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Sighten
providers.description: Sighten was a San Francisco software company, backed by Obvious Ventures, that built a cloud platform for the residential and commercial solar industry — covering system design, proposal generation, sales, and financing workflows used by solar installers, dealers, and finance providers. The Sighten business was acquired (by GoodLeap) and folded into EverBright; the original sighten.io domain now redirects to goeverbright.com. EverBright operates as a residential solar and home-battery financing platform, connecting homeowners with local installers through lease and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) products and the MyEverBright monitoring portal. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published for the Sighten or EverBright brand; a partner-facing platform (engine.goeverbright.com) and a protected API host (api.goeverbright.com, HTTP 401) exist but are not publicly documented. This profile records the company's current, honest public surface after enrichment.

providers.name: Growatt
providers.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

providers.name: Astronergy
providers.description: Astronergy (Chint New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.) is the photovoltaic cell and module manufacturing arm of China's CHINT Group. Founded in 2006, it is one of the earliest private Chinese enterprises in the PV sector and is ranked among the world's largest module suppliers. It designs, manufactures and sells high-efficiency crystalline-silicon PV cells and modules — notably the n-type TOPCon ASTRO N series in bifacial and monofacial form — for utility-scale power stations, commercial and industrial rooftops, and residential systems. Astronergy sells into more than 140 countries and regions and operates manufacturing bases and sales centers in markets including Germany, Spain, the USA, Brazil and Turkey. Its public web surface is a marketing and product-download site: datasheets, installation manuals, warranty and certification PDFs, a module-authenticity checker and a PV Planner yield calculator. It publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Dandelion Energy
providers.description: Dandelion Energy is a residential geothermal heating and cooling company that designs, engineers, and installs ground-source heat pump systems for homeowners and new-home builders. Its systems tap the earth's stable subsurface temperature to heat and cool homes year-round, cutting utility bills and carbon emissions versus conventional fossil-fuel HVAC. Dandelion delivers end-to-end service from ground-loop drilling through turnkey installation, and offers a leasing program that removes the upfront cost for buyers. The company reports thousands of installations across the United States. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the frontier-tech and climate sector; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Gecko Robotics
providers.description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based AI and robotics company that inspects and manages critical physical infrastructure. Its wall-climbing, aerial and submersible robots capture full-coverage ultrasonic, visual and other sensor readings from boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, pipelines, ship hulls and decks, which are fused with facility records and operational data inside Cantilever, the company's AI-powered operating platform for the built world. Cantilever quantifies corrosion rates, predicts remaining asset life and prioritizes capital and maintenance decisions for customers across defense, power, oil and gas, steel, pulp and paper, mining and advanced manufacturing. Cantilever is delivered as a closed, authenticated enterprise SaaS at cantilever.app; Gecko Robotics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or self-serve API program, and integrations are arranged through the company directly.

providers.name: Constellation Energy
providers.description: Constellation Energy Corporation is a Fortune 500 clean-energy producer and competitive retail electricity and natural gas supplier in the United States, generating power from a fleet of nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar facilities. Constellation does not publish a public developer portal; programmatic interactions are delivered to enterprise and large commercial customers through the Energy Manager platform (account-managed onboarding, no public API specifications) and consumer interactions are handled through the My Constellation account portal. EDI 867 (usage) and 810 (invoice) remain the most common machine-to-machine integration paths and are arranged on a contract-by-contract basis.

providers.name: Bonnet
providers.description: Bonnet is a UK-based electric vehicle (EV) charging app that aggregates multiple charging networks into a single platform, letting drivers find, access, and pay for chargers across Europe through one membership. Headquartered in Bristol and acquired by OVO Energy, it gives consumers real-time charger status, route planning, membership plans with per-charge savings, and weekly charging-credit rewards, while offering charge point operator (CPO) and fleet solutions with white-label integration for businesses. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Bonnet publishes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Eliq
providers.description: Eliq provides energy data and analytics APIs for utilities and energy app developers. The platform combines a decade of analytics and machine learning trained on millions of homes to deliver consumption insights, disaggregation, forecasting, peak detection, tariff comparison, and customer segmentation.

providers.name: Evie Networks
providers.description: Evie Networks is an Australian electric-vehicle charging infrastructure company, founded in 2017 and backed by the St Baker Energy Innovation Fund, that owns and operates one of the country's largest DC fast and ultrafast public charging networks across 300+ locations in every state and territory. It sits downstream of the electricity retail market as a charge point operator (CPO) and e-mobility service provider, buying energy and reselling it as charging sessions to drivers and fleets, and it also builds and operates charging assets for site hosts, councils, dealerships and commercial property owners. Its API posture is closed: as of 2026-07-27 there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no named support for the EV charging interoperability standards (OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118). Evie is not a designated data holder under Australia's Consumer Data Right energy regime — the CDR Register's public energy data-holder brand summary lists 84 brands and Evie is not among them — so the statutory data mandate that produced identical APIs across Australian banks and energy retailers does not reach the EV charging layer at all. A live production API host exists at api.goevie.com.au serving the Evie Charging mobile app, but it is undocumented, unadvertised and returns a Google Cloud Endpoints 404 to anonymous callers. Neither consumer charging-session data nor network/market data is published through any documented public interface; charger location data reaches developers only through third-party aggregators.

providers.name: Heirloom
providers.description: Heirloom Carbon Technologies, Inc. is a San Francisco Bay Area direct air capture (DAC) company that removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere by accelerating the natural mineralization of limestone. Heirloom spreads calcium oxide on vertical trays where it re-absorbs atmospheric CO2 in days rather than years, then uses electric kilns to release the captured CO2 for permanent geologic or in-concrete storage. The company opened the first commercial DAC facility in the United States, sells permanent carbon removal credits to individuals, businesses and enterprises, and has signed offtake agreements with Microsoft, Frontier, United's Sustainable Flight Fund and CarbonCure. It is an industrial climate-technology company; it does not operate a public developer program or API.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Delek US Holdings
providers.description: Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK) is a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. Logistics assets are operated through Delek Logistics Partners (NYSE: DKL). The company provides investor relations and ESG reporting on its public website but does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

providers.name: Southern Company
providers.description: Southern Company is an Atlanta-headquartered energy holding company and one of the largest producers of electricity in the United States, serving approximately 9 million electric and natural gas customers through Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Mississippi Power, Southern Power, Southern Company Gas (Atlanta Gas Light, Nicor Gas, Virginia Natural Gas, Chattanooga Gas), Southern Nuclear, PowerSecure, Southern Linc and Southern Telecom. It sits at the vertically-integrated regulated-utility layer of the value chain — it owns generation, transmission and distribution, operates its own balancing authority rather than belonging to an ISO/RTO, and runs a FERC-approved bid-based energy auction for wholesale power in the Southeast. Its API posture is honestly closed on both sides of the sector's two-speed split. There is no consumer data mandate in Alabama, Georgia or Mississippi and Southern Company does not implement Green Button Download My Data or Connect My Data, is not listed by the Green Button Alliance, and publishes no ESPI endpoint — a customer can only export their own interval data as a spreadsheet after logging into My Power Usage, and a third party gets billing history only through a signed paper release form. On the market side the FERC-required auction clearing prices and weighted-average hour-ahead transaction prices are posted as public web pages, but they are JavaScript-rendered HTML with no CSV, no feed and no API behind them. A production Apigee API gateway is live at api.southernco.com and developer.southernco.com resolves behind an Imperva edge, so the platform machinery exists internally, but no proxy, no specification and no documentation are published to anyone outside the company.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
providers.description: Optivolt Labs (operating as Optivolt) is a Burlingame, California solar technology company building intelligent home solar systems with power electronics embedded directly inside each panel. Its patented Balancer device shuffles power from stronger to weaker zones within a panel to keep energy flowing in shaded and non-ideal conditions, delivering up to 50% more annual energy and improved shaded performance versus conventional panels. The product line includes 450W N-type mono half-cut panels, universal battery and inverter compatibility, and a real-time monitoring app for tracking energy and savings. Optivolt is a Techstars-backed hardware company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Papernest
providers.description: Papernest is a French technology company, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Paris, that provides a digital platform for managing, switching, and cancelling household subscriptions — energy, telecom and internet, mobile plans, and home insurance — through a single interface. Built around the moment people move home, the service is free to end users and monetized through commissions from supplier partners across France, Spain, Italy, and the UK, having helped more than 3 million customers. Papernest does not publish a public developer API; it runs a private B2B partner integration program and maintains an official GitHub organization of archived open-source utilities.

providers.name: SM Energy
providers.description: SM Energy Company (NYSE: SM) is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Founded in 1908 (originally as St. Mary Land & Exploration Company), SM Energy focuses on acquiring, exploring, developing, and producing crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids (NGLs) from top-tier assets across the Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico, the Maverick Basin in South Texas, the DJ Basin in Colorado, and the Uinta Basin in northeast Utah. The company is a Fortune 1000 member with approximately 1,241 employees and average daily net production of 206.8 MBoe/d. SM Energy completed a merger with Civitas Resources in early 2026. The company does not offer a public developer API; investor data is accessible through financial data APIs and SEC EDGAR.

providers.name: APA Corporation
providers.description: APA Corporation is an independent energy company that explores for, develops, and produces natural gas, crude oil, and natural gas liquids, with operations in the United States, Egypt, the United Kingdom, and Suriname. Organized in Delaware and headquartered in Houston, Texas, APA is listed on Nasdaq (APA) and listed on Nasdaq Texas since March 2026.

providers.name: Enurgen
providers.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Boldr
providers.description: Boldr is a Techstars-backed consumer hardware company building energy-saving smart home climate control devices. Its two products are Kelvin, a smart infrared heater, and Klima, a smart thermostat controller for mini-split air conditioners that also monitors appliance health so units last longer with fewer issues. Both devices are managed through the Boldr mobile app, which lets homeowners control climate settings remotely and track energy usage to lower utility bills. Boldr also runs Boldr Pro, a program for HVAC contractors. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted online store at shopboldr.com and does not currently publish a first-party developer API; its only public machine-readable surface is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery served at the storefront host.

providers.name: Gridware
providers.description: Gridware builds grid intelligence technology for electric utilities. Its Active Grid Response (AGR) platform pairs pole-mounted GridScope sensors with analytics to bring real-time visibility into the physical, electrical, and environmental condition of every span of the distribution grid, closing the "Hazard Awareness Delay" between when a fault or hazard occurs and when a utility detects it. Gridware supports fault prevention, faster power restoration, wildfire and hazard response, and grid asset management. Headquartered in San Francisco with an Applied Research Complex in Richmond, California, the company is backed by True Ventures. Gridware does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity, trust/compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: SkySpecs
providers.description: SkySpecs is a renewable energy asset management company based in Ann Arbor, Michigan that combines autonomous drone inspections, condition-monitoring hardware, and its cloud-based Horizon software platform to help wind and solar operators manage the health and performance of their assets. Horizon consolidates blade inspection imagery, drivetrain and sensor data, SCADA-based performance analytics, repair-vendor coordination, and financial reporting into one hub, with third-party data ingestion and custom integrations for fleet owners. The company reports assets under contract across six countries and is backed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management. SkySpecs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or self-serve developer portal today; integrations are arranged directly with the Horizon team.

providers.name: GE Vernova
providers.description: GE Vernova is accelerating the path to more reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy through its innovative portfolio of electrification, power, and decarbonization technologies. Spun off from General Electric, GE Vernova brings together the legacy GE Power, Renewable Energy, Digital, and Energy Financial Services businesses to help solve the world's energy transition challenges.

providers.name: General Fusion
providers.description: General Fusion is a Canadian fusion energy company founded in 2002 by physicist Dr. Michel Laberge and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia, in the Vancouver area. It is developing Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF), an approach that combines plasma formation, mechanical compression by a liquid metal liner, and practical heat capture for electricity generation. The company operates LM26, which it describes as the world's largest and most powerful operational fusion plasma injector, and reports 24 plasma prototypes, more than 200,000 plasma experiments, 35+ peer-reviewed papers, and roughly 210 issued and pending patents. In July 2026 General Fusion completed a business combination with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III and became the first publicly listed fusion energy company, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker GFUZ. It is an energy hardware and research company rather than a software or API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts. Its only machine-readable public surfaces are a Yoast-generated llms.txt and the WordPress REST discovery index behind its marketing site.

providers.name: Gridwiz
providers.description: Gridwiz Inc. is a South Korean clean-energy software and hardware company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seoul. It operates one of Korea's largest demand response (DR) aggregation portfolios, gathering electricity that industrial and commercial customers curtail and selling it into the national power market, and it pairs that with energy storage (ESS), renewable energy / RE100 and PPA advisory, and an e-mobility line covering EV charging controllers, CCS communication modems (EVCC/SECC), bidirectional V2G chargers and the Skyblue consumer charging service. Its e-mobility products are built to the international EV charging standards DIN SPEC 70121, ISO 15118 (including 15118-20 AC/DC) and OCPP, and its demand response management system is described as OpenADR-based. Gridwiz sells energy services and certified hardware to utilities, EVSE suppliers and enterprises; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Husk Power Systems
providers.description: Husk Power Systems is an energy technology company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Fort Collins, Colorado with operating hubs in Patna, Mumbai and Pune (India) and Abuja (Nigeria), that builds, owns and operates AI-enabled distributed renewable energy systems — community solar minigrids, commercial and industrial solar, and residential rooftop — for unserved and underserved communities, businesses and households across Africa and Asia. Husk operates one of the largest minigrid fleets in the world and pairs it with pay-as-you-go smart metering, a customer mobile app (HUSKify) and an internal operations platform (Husk Neuron). Its software is delivered as end-user and operator products; Husk publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Omnidian
providers.description: Omnidian, Inc. is a Seattle-based clean energy performance assurance company, founded in 2015, that protects and accelerates investments in residential and commercial solar and battery storage. Its proprietary, machine-learning driven software platform continuously monitors distributed solar assets, diagnoses hardware, communication and environmental faults such as soiling, shading and snow, dispatches a nationwide field service technician network across 48 states, Washington D.C. and Puerto Rico, and underwrites a 95% energy production guarantee that reimburses owners for covered shortfalls. Omnidian serves installers, EPCs, developers, IPPs, solar financing providers, commercial real estate owners and asset investors, and is a Certified B Corporation and a member of the SunSpec Alliance. Its monitoring platform, client portal and field service partner portal are operated as private, authenticated systems; Omnidian publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Quaise Energy
providers.description: Quaise Energy is a deep-geothermal energy company and MIT spinout, founded in 2018 by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde out of a decade of millimeter-wave research by Paul Woskov at the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center. Quaise is developing millimeter-wave (MMW) drilling — using a gyrotron to vaporize rather than grind rock — to reach supercritical conditions several kilometers down, where temperatures approach 500 degrees C, and to convert existing fossil-fuel power stations to superhot geothermal baseload. The company drilled 100 meters with the technique at its Central Texas field site in 2025. Quaise is an energy and hardware company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public web application is a levelized-cost-of-energy (LCOE) calculator whose full functionality sits behind an AWS Cognito login.

providers.name: Airspace Intelligence
providers.description: Air Space Intelligence (ASI) builds AI software for mission-critical, geospatial operations across aviation, defense, logistics, and energy. Its Prescience platform fuses data, models operational domains, runs predictive simulations, and optimizes complex operations in real time — spanning airline operations, air traffic management, global logistics, defense (space, air, land, sea), and energy grids. ASI holds an $875M FAA contract to help modernize the U.S. National Airspace System and works with partners including Alaska Airlines, National Grid, and the U.S. Air Force. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Atom Power
providers.description: Atom Power, Inc. is a Charlotte, North Carolina electrical technology company founded in 2014 that invented the Atom Switch, the world's first commercial UL-listed digital solid-state circuit breaker. The company builds SiC (silicon carbide) power modules, solid-state switchgear and panel-level Level 2 electric-vehicle charging hardware for commercial, industrial, data-center and grid-edge deployments, paired with cloud software for energy management, load balancing and charger operations. Atom Power previously ran an "Atom Cloud" developer portal on Azure API Management at developers.atompower.com with a gateway at api.atompower.com; both hostnames are now dangling CNAMEs to deleted Azure API Management instances, so no public API contract is currently reachable.

providers.name: Choose Energy
providers.description: Choose Energy is a free online energy marketplace, founded in 2008 and operated by Red Ventures, that helps consumers and businesses in deregulated U.S. energy markets compare electricity and natural gas plans, view transparent all-inclusive pricing, and switch providers online in minutes. The platform serves customers across Texas, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois, New Jersey, New York, Maryland, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and other deregulated states, and also offers solar cost estimation, business energy procurement, and educational energy resources. Choose Energy is a consumer-facing web marketplace and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: MayMaan Research
providers.description: MayMaan Research is a clean-energy engineering company that redesigns the internal combustion engine around its patented AquaStroke platform, a piston engine that runs on a blend of roughly 70% water and 30% bio-alcohol (ethanol or methanol) instead of gasoline or diesel. The company builds modular generator sets and powertrains that scale from a 35 kW unit (A35) through the AV2 to multi-megawatt installations, and it positions them as drop-in replacements for diesel gensets in power generation, EV charging infrastructure, data centers, telecommunications, marine, construction, agriculture, defense and off-grid deployments, with near-zero NOx, SOx, CO2 and particulate output. MayMaan is headquartered in Hollywood, Florida with a European office in Paris, holds engine and fuel-system patents internationally, and raised a $30 million Series A led by WAVE Equity Partners. It is a hardware manufacturer: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Meshcrafts
providers.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

providers.name: MoveYou
providers.description: Our scaled based platform meets all your business requirements in the fields of mobility and energy. Explore the powerful solutions or consult one of our experts for advice. Together, we are building a sustainable future for your organization.

providers.name: Ohmium
providers.description: Ohmium International designs, manufactures and deploys modular, vertically-stackable proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer systems for cost-competitive green hydrogen production. Its Lotus PEM electrolyzer platform integrates power electronics, water treatment and controls into skid-mounted modules for industrial, energy and mobility customers, and is paired with EPC and remote monitoring and maintenance (RM&M) services. Ohmium is a hardware and clean-energy engineering company: it publishes no public developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable specification, and its customer-facing monitoring and service portals are third-party SaaS products hosted on Ohmium subdomains behind login.

providers.name: Solaren
providers.description: Solaren is a combination energy and aerospace company headquartered in Manhattan Beach, California, founded in 2001 by a team of satellite engineers and space scientists. Solaren designs, develops, integrates, deploys and operates space solar power (SSP) plants: solar arrays on a patented lightweight solar power satellite in geosynchronous orbit convert sunlight to electricity, convert that electricity to radio-frequency power, and beam it to an earth receiving station that returns it to the grid as baseload power. The company's business model is to own and operate its SSP plants and sell continuous, zero-emission electricity to utility and government customers; it signed the world's first power purchase agreement for space solar electricity, with Pacific Gas & Electric. Solaren is a hardware and energy-generation company and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Utilidata
providers.description: Utilidata is an Ann Arbor, Michigan software company building Karman, a distributed AI platform that runs on a custom NVIDIA system-on-module embedded directly into electrical infrastructure — smart meters and grid-edge devices on the utility side, PDUs and power trays inside AI data centers. Karman processes high-resolution AC metrology locally (single-cycle waveform statistics at 1+ MS/s sample rates) to produce "data products" such as Power Quality Analytics, enabling millisecond-level power control, GPU/PSU failure prediction, phase balancing and power-aware scheduling. Utilidata publishes the Karman Power Aware Module as Apache-2.0 open source: a Rust reference implementation that serializes Karman data products as Protocol Buffers (package utilidata.karman.bibimbap.v1), transports them over ZeroMQ, and exposes them to Prometheus and TimescaleDB through a Helm-packaged Kubernetes stack. The company has raised a $100M Series C and counts NVIDIA, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, American Electric Power and Renown Capital Partners among its backers.

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
providers.description: SLB (Schlumberger) is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The SLB (Schlumberger) API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: CenterPoint Energy
providers.description: CenterPoint Energy is a domestic energy delivery company that provides electric transmission and distribution, natural gas distribution, and energy services operations serving residential, commercial, and industrial customers across multiple U.S. states. Developer-facing interfaces include the Smart Meter Texas (SMT) Usage History Inquiry API, Green Button Connect My Data exports for authorized third-party access to customer interval usage, and the Centerpoint Connect service API at api-portal.centerpointconnect.io used by contractor and field-service integrations.

providers.name: CONSOL Energy
providers.description: CONSOL Energy was a Pittsburgh-based coal mining company that produced high-quality bituminous coal from underground mines for sale to electric utilities, steelmakers, and industrial customers. In 2025 CONSOL Energy merged with Arch Resources to form Core Natural Resources, and the consolenergy.com domain now redirects to corenaturalresources.com. The combined company does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations site, a suppliers page (with downloadable terms, conditions, and a Supplier Code of Conduct), and corporate sustainability/safety disclosures — all HTML and PDF, with no documented endpoints and no XML feeds (probed 2026-07-25). Those pages are listed below as website surfaces, not as APIs. The only verified programmatic access to this company's data is the SEC's own EDGAR APIs. See the sibling profile arch-coal for the other half of the merger.

providers.name: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux)
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is an American orbital-infrastructure company founded in 2024 by Baiju Bhatt, co-founder and former co-CEO of Robinhood, headquartered in San Carlos, California with a second site in Seattle, Washington. It operated as Aetherflux Inc. from founding until May 2026, when it renamed to Cowboy Space Corporation and broadened its mission from space-based solar power alone to vertically integrated orbital infrastructure for the AI era, spanning launch vehicles, space-based power generation and in-orbit compute. Its flagship program is Stampede, a Low Earth Orbit constellation of satellites that harvest solar power to run on-orbit GPU data centers, with the first Galactic Brain data-center node targeted for early 2027 using NVIDIA Space-1 Vera Rubin modules and a small infrared power-beaming demonstrator satellite planned for 2026. The company concluded that launch supply was the binding constraint on orbital compute and is therefore also developing its own rocket, sized between Falcon 9 and Starship at roughly 20,000-25,000 kg of payload, whose upper stage is itself the payload - each one intended to become a one-megawatt orbital data center - with a first launch targeted for the end of 2028. It has raised roughly USD 365 million to date, including a USD 50 million Series A in April 2025 and a USD 275 million Series B in May 2026 at a USD 2 billion valuation, led by Index Ventures with IVP, Blossom Capital, SAIC, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA and Interlagos participating. Cowboy Space is a space hardware and energy infrastructure company, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no public GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its entire public web presence is a four-page Framer-hosted marketing site (home, terms, privacy, media terms of use) plus an Ashby-hosted careers board.

providers.name: Jaipur Robotics
providers.description: Jaipur Robotics is a Manno, Switzerland based deep-tech company building advanced computer vision and deep learning solutions for the waste-to-energy sector. Its product, Jaipur Intelligence, applies patent-pending image recognition to plant bunkers and truck unloading bays to detect oversized and dangerous items, map the calorific value (LHV) of incoming waste in real time, and track crane operations — helping operators cut emissions, improve waste mixing and combustion stability, and minimize unplanned shutdowns. The company operates a gated customer application at app.jaipurrobotics.com and is backed by Techstars, Innosuisse, Venture Kick, CSEM and others. It currently publishes a marketing site and a customer login only; there is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Plural Finance
providers.description: Plural Finance is a financial operating system for infrastructure — a programmable execution layer that automates ownership, payments, compliance, and reporting across the lifecycle of infrastructure and energy assets. Its AssetOS platform tokenizes infrastructure assets such as distributed renewables, data centers, public-private partnerships, and electricity sales contracts, so institutional and individual investors can underwrite, monitor, and trade projects, with smart-contract execution of capital contributions and distributions and embedded regulatory controls. The company holds broker-dealer licensing and is backed by Paradigm. Plural currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is through its institutional web application.

providers.name: Bechtel
providers.description: Bechtel is one of the largest privately held engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) companies in the world. Bechtel does not publish a public developer portal; technology integration is delivered through project-specific data exchanges with owners, joint-venture partners, and subcontractors, the Bechtel supplier portal, and industry-standard construction data exchange formats (IFC, COBie, CDE) over secure project-management platforms.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Murphy USA
providers.description: Murphy USA (NYSE: MUSA) is a Fortune 500 retailer of gasoline and convenience merchandise, headquartered in El Dorado, Arkansas. The company operates roughly 1,700 Murphy USA and Murphy Express stores across a 27-state footprint in the southern and midwestern United States, most of them sited in or adjacent to Walmart Supercenter parking lots, and it also owns the QuickChek chain of fresh convenience stores in New Jersey and New York. Its fuel slate spans E-10, E-15, FlexFuel (E85), ethanol-free E0, ULSD diesel, biodiesel and winterized diesel, marketed alongside a FuelAssure fuel-quality monitoring program. Consumer digital engagement runs through the Murphy Drive Rewards loyalty app and a Business Fuel Card program. Murphy USA publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Sempra Energy
providers.description: Sempra Energy is a San Diego-headquartered North American energy infrastructure holding company and a Fortune 500 constituent, operating regulated utilities and energy infrastructure across California, Texas and Mexico. Its businesses include San Diego Gas & Electric and Southern California Gas Company in California, Oncor Electric Delivery in Texas, and Sempra Infrastructure, which develops LNG export terminals, natural gas pipelines and renewable generation in North America. Sempra operates a Google Apigee API program — an API gateway at api.sempra.com and a developer portal at developer.sempra.com inviting developers to "sign up today and start using Sempra APIs" — but publishes no API product, contract or reference to unauthenticated visitors, so the entire integration surface sits behind portal registration.

providers.name: Aalo Atomics
providers.description: Aalo Atomics is an Austin, Texas-based advanced nuclear engineering company, founded in 2021, working to make reactor deployment fast, repeatable, and economical through factory manufacturing. It is developing the Aalo-1, a factory-fabricated sodium-cooled microreactor (~10 MWe class), and Aalo Pod power plants that combine five Aalo-1 reactors to deliver roughly 50 megawatts of electricity for data centers, industrial facilities, and communities. The company describes a new XMR ("extra modular reactor") category, has raised a $100M Series B, and is advancing through U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission pre-application activities and a U.S. Department of Energy experimental microreactor site in Idaho. This API Evangelist profile tracks Aalo Atomics as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: American Superconductor Corporation
providers.description: American Superconductor Corporation (AMSC) is a Ayer, Massachusetts based power systems company that designs and deploys grid interconnection, power protection, and power supply solutions for the energy, renewables, industrial, utility, and military sectors. Its portfolio spans grid systems such as D-VAR dynamic reactive compensation and STATCOM, ship protection and degaussing systems for naval defense, wind turbine electrical control systems, and Amperium high-temperature superconductor wire. AMSC was surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a public-company / hardtech profile with no public developer API surface; the enrichment pass captured domain-security posture and corporate link properties only.

providers.name: Amogy
providers.description: Amogy is an energy-technology company decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors by converting energy-dense ammonia into dispatchable, zero-carbon electricity. Its AMMDrive power systems crack ammonia into hydrogen and nitrogen and convert the hydrogen to power for data centers, industrial facilities, microgrids, and maritime vessels, and it develops proprietary low-temperature ammonia-cracking catalysts. Backed by DCVC and other investors, Amogy has demonstrated the world's first carbon-free ammonia-powered maritime vessel and partners with firms such as Samsung Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Amogy publishes no public developer API surface at this time, so this record captures its corporate identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: AMSC
providers.description: American Superconductor Corporation (AMSC) is a power control systems company headquartered in Ayer, Massachusetts, and traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker AMSC. The company designs and delivers grid and power-electronics solutions across three specialties - power supply, power protection, and power innovation - serving the energy, renewables, utility, industrial, materials, and military sectors. Its offerings span grid capacity and resiliency systems, renewable generation integration, industrial process power control, and shipboard power protection for naval defense. AMSC is an early Battery Ventures portfolio investment. AMSC does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's corporate identity and domain security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Battery Smart
providers.description: Battery Smart is India's largest battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, founded in 2019 by Pulkit Khurana and Siddharth Sikka and operated from New Delhi by Upgrid Solutions Private Limited and Upgrid Electrilease Private Limited. It runs an asset-light, partner-led model: local businesses — kirana stores, petrol pumps and neighbourhood shops — host swap points where a driver exchanges a depleted lithium-ion pack for a charged one in roughly two minutes and pays per swap instead of buying the battery with the vehicle, which removes the single largest cost from an electric two- or three-wheeler. The network is concentrated in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow, and the company has raised across eleven rounds including a USD 65 million Series B led by LeapFrog Investments with MUFG Bank, Panasonic, Ecosystem Integrity Fund, Blume Ventures and British International Investment participating, plus a USD 15 million debt round with Mirova in April 2026. Battery Smart's software ships only as end-user Android applications — Battery Smart Driver and Battery Smart Partner — backed by a production API host at api.upgrid.in that self-identifies as the "Battery Smart API". As of this profile the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Bloom Energy
providers.description: Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) is a San Jose, California hardtech company that designs and manufactures solid-oxide fuel cell "Energy Server" platforms which generate electricity on-site from natural gas, biogas, or hydrogen through an electrochemical process rather than combustion. Its modular systems deliver resilient, always-on power for data centers, manufacturing, healthcare, utilities, and critical infrastructure, can be deployed in roughly 90 days, and scale from single units to hundreds of megawatts. Bloom also builds high-temperature solid-oxide electrolyzers for low-cost hydrogen production. The company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a hardtech portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Bolt.Earth
providers.description: Bolt.Earth operates what it describes as India's largest EV charging network, with more than 100,000 charging points deployed across 2,100+ cities. The company sells EV charging hardware (3.3kW smart sockets for 2/3/4-wheelers, AC chargers from 7.4kW to 22kW, and DC fast chargers from 30kW to 240kW) alongside a Charging Management System (CMS) for operators and a consumer mobile app for locating, booking, and paying for charging sessions. Services span site assessment, installation, KYC onboarding, charger activation, remote firmware updates, and 24/7 support for individuals, RWAs, enterprises, fleet operators, hospitality venues, highways, and government agencies. Bolt.Earth is backed by Version One Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an energy-sector company profile. No public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Capstone Turbine
providers.description: Capstone Turbine Corporation, now operating as Capstone Green Energy (and its operating entity Capstone Energy+), is a California-based manufacturer of low-emission microturbine energy systems founded in 1988. The company designs and builds oil-free, air-bearing microturbines ranging from 65 kW to multi-megawatt configurations for on-site and on-demand power, combined heat and power (CHP), and combined cooling, heat and power (CCHP). Its systems power data centers, microgrids, ports, EV charging, oil and gas operations, critical power, and renewable energy applications. Capstone was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Enter
providers.description: Enter is a Berlin-based residential energy-efficiency company that positions itself as Germany's largest energy advisor, combining on-site building analysis with installation of heat pumps, photovoltaic (solar) systems, battery storage, EV wallboxes, and home energy-management systems. It guides homeowners through energy consulting, subsidy (Foerderung) applications, and financing, and reports 37,000+ completed projects and 150M+ EUR in secured subsidies. Enter is a B2C service provider with no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; it was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: LF Energy
providers.description: LF Energy is a Linux Foundation project building open source technology solutions for the power grid and energy sector. Launched in 2018, it accelerates the energy transition through open source collaboration and hosts projects for grid modernization, flexibility, and decarbonization.

providers.name: Mazama Energy
providers.description: Mazama Energy is a geothermal energy company reinventing power generation with enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) that tap superhot rock to deliver universal, scalable, clean, and affordable electricity. Its Thermal Lattice sequential-stimulation technology improves connectivity between injectors and producers in super hot reservoirs (SHR). The company is developing the Newberry project in Oregon and runs the Mazama EMPOWER program, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Prisma Photonics
providers.description: Prisma Photonics is an infrastructure-monitoring company that turns existing optical fiber into a continuous sensing network using its Hyper-Scan Fiber-Sensing distributed acoustic sensing technology. The platform measures strain, temperature, pressure, and acoustic signatures at every point along hundreds of kilometers of fiber with sub-meter resolution, and applies AI-driven classification to detect and identify events in real time. It is used to protect and monitor power lines, oil and gas pipelines, perimeters, subsea assets, and smart rail and road infrastructure. Backed by Insight Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Sage Geosystems
providers.description: Sage Geosystems is a Houston, Texas energy company developing "Pressure Geothermal" — an evolution of traditional geothermal that applies subsurface breakthroughs from the oil and gas industry to hot dry rock. Its two-well Power Generation system circulates water through engineered "lung" fractures and extracts heat at surface through a heat exchanger driving an sCO2 turbine, while its single-well EarthStore energy storage system charges and discharges over 8-hour to multi-day timescales for long-duration storage. The company markets to utilities, data centers and government partners rather than to developers: as of this profile it operates a seven-page marketing site with no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: SOLS Energy
providers.description: SOLS Energy is Malaysia's leading residential and commercial solar energy company, on a mission to make green energy a basic human right. It has completed more than 8,900 solar installations across Malaysia spanning residential (Green Homes), commercial (Green Business), and off-grid indigenous community projects (Green Impact), and also offers EV charging (ChargeSingh) and a Solar Academy apprenticeship program. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass SOLS Energy publishes a consumer marketing website (blog, FAQ, contact, privacy and terms pages) but no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Star Catcher
providers.description: Star Catcher is a space technology company building the first power grid in space. Its optical power beaming system, the Star Catcher Network, concentrates and transmits solar energy directly to satellites' existing solar arrays, delivering up to 10x more power without any hardware modifications. Founded in 2024 and backed by Initialized Capital, the company holds a world record for optical power beaming and is working to bring shared orbital power infrastructure to satellites supporting universal connectivity, advanced computing, and national security. Star Catcher raised $65 million in May 2026 and plans to bring its technology to orbit. Star Catcher operates physical space hardware and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Swift Charge
providers.description: Swift Charge is an electric vehicle charging company that provides turn-key, fully managed EV charging infrastructure to property owners across the hospitality, education, and multi-family residential sectors, pairing installed charging hardware with a payment application that lets EV drivers locate and pay for charging sessions. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Swift Charge publishes a public marketing and charger-map website but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile is limited to company identity plus a domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: Tiger New Energy
providers.description: Tiger New Energy is a Bangladesh-based clean-energy company building a battery-swapping network for electric vehicles, primarily electric rickshaws and motorcycles. Drivers swap depleted lithium batteries for fully charged ones at Tiger swapping stations in seconds instead of waiting to recharge, and a "battery passport" tracks each pack's health and lifecycle. The company operates consumer and partner mobile apps (Tiger Driver, Tiger Partner, Tiger Dealer) on iOS and Android. Tiger New Energy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its mobile apps are backed by private, undocumented services.

providers.name: Upwing Energy
providers.description: Upwing Energy is an energy technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cerritos, California, with service operations near Houston, Texas, operating as an affiliate of Calnetix Technologies. It designs, manufactures and deploys the Subsurface Compressor System (SCS) — a downhole gas compressor installed up to two miles inside a natural gas well — along with Magnetic Drive Systems and the supporting high-speed permanent magnet motors, passive magnetic radial bearings, active magnetic thrust bearings, magnetic couplings and sensorless long-step-out variable speed drives that make it work. The company sells hardware and an end-to-end field service (planning and completions, deployment and startup, operations and monitoring, analysis and predictions) to natural gas operators worldwide, including deployments with Equinor, ENAP and operators across MENA and Central Asia. It publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: CF Industries Holdings
providers.description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

providers.name: RPC
providers.description: RPC, Inc. is an oilfield services company providing specialized well services to independent and major oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration, production, and development of oil and gas properties. Operating through subsidiaries including Cudd Energy Services, Patterson Services, Spinnaker Oilwell Services, and Thru Tubing Solutions, RPC offers pressure pumping, wireline, downhole tools, coiled tubing, cementing, snubbing, nitrogen services, well control, rental tools, and tubular services. RPC does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Air Company
providers.description: Air Company (AIRCO) is a carbon conversion technology company founded in 2017 by Gregory Constantine and Dr. Stafford Sheehan. Its patented Carbon Conversion Reactor mimics photosynthesis, combining captured CO2, water and green hydrogen with renewable energy to produce carbon-negative alcohols and fully formulated synthetic fuels. The company licenses its catalytic process technologies and designs deployable production systems, from the container-scale AIRCO MAD Fuel System to the AIRCO SAF Factory. Product lines are branded AIRMADE and span sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), ethanol, methanol, diesel and rocket fuel, with earlier consumer validation products including AIR Vodka and AIR Eau de Parfum.
