Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Air Force, Department of Energy and NASA, alongside aviation partners such as Virgin, Air France-KLM, JetBlue and Air Canada; strategic investors include Alaska Airlines, Carbon Direct, In-Q-Tel and Toyota Ventures. Air Company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract as of the 2026-07-31 enrichment pass.

providers.name: Electric Hydrogen
providers.description: Electric Hydrogen (EH2) is a Massachusetts-based clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and commissions the world's most powerful PEM electrolyzers, packaged into a fully-integrated 100MW HYPRPlant that turns water and renewable electricity into the lowest-cost green hydrogen. The complete plant solution bundles power conversion, gas processing, water treatment, and thermal management so heavy industry can decarbonize ammonia, e-fuels, steel, and refining at gigawatt scale. Founded in 2020 and led by CEO Raffi Garabedian, EH2 operates a 1.2GW gigafactory in Devens, Massachusetts, became green hydrogen's first unicorn with a $380M Series C, and is backed by Fifth Wall, Fortescue, Energy Impact Partners, bp Ventures, Temasek, and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund. This profile enriches the API Evangelist network stub with the company's real public web surface.

providers.name: Lila Sciences
providers.description: Lila Sciences is an AI company founded in 2023 that is building what it calls Scientific Superintelligence: an autonomous system that runs the scientific method end to end by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, executing them in physical AI Science Factories (autonomous robotic laboratory networks), and learning from the resulting experimental data. Rather than training on internet text, Lila trains a scientific reasoning model on experimental data, coupling it to scalable verifiers and instruments such as molecular dynamics simulators, protein structure predictors, quantum chemistry solvers, and gene editors, then optimizing the policy with reinforcement learning. The company packages this as two commercial offerings: Catalyst, positioned as an operating system for science that accelerates an organization's existing research, and Creation, a partnership model for generating new discoveries, launching products, and founding new companies. Lila works across therapeutics (mRNA, proteins, antibodies, cell therapies, small molecules), advanced materials, chemicals, energy and environment, oil and gas, aerospace and defense, and biotech. It has raised roughly $550M ($200M seed announced March 2025 and a $350M Series A closed in October 2025) from investors including General Catalyst and NVIDIA, at a reported valuation above $1.3B, and collaborates with NVIDIA on the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit. Lila operates from Cambridge MA, San Francisco CA, and London UK. As of this profile Lila publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this entry is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sunfire
providers.description: Sunfire SE is a German hydrogen technology manufacturer headquartered in Dresden, Saxony, with additional sites in Berlin and Solingen. Founded in 2010 by Carl Berninghausen, Christian von Olshausen and Nils Aldag, and converted to a European stock corporation (SE) in 2025, the company builds industrial-scale electrolyzers and power-to-X plants that convert renewable electricity into green hydrogen and synthetic fuels. Its Sunfire-HyLink portfolio spans pressurized alkaline electrolysis (HyLink Alkaline 22 at 10 MW and HyLink Alkaline 23 at 50 MW per module, operating at 30 bar(g)) and high-temperature solid oxide electrolysis (HyLink SOEC, 10 MW modules, a claimed world-record 37.5 kWh/kg H2 efficiency), alongside FEED engineering, project delivery, maintenance and remote data-driven monitoring services. Customers and projects include RWE, Salzgitter, Neste, TotalEnergies, BASF, P2X Solutions, Nordic Ren-Gas and the Bad Lauchstaedt Energy Park. Sunfire is an industrial equipment manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: SHINE Technologies
providers.description: SHINE Technologies is a privately held fusion technology company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Janesville, Wisconsin, that operates fusion neutron generators at industrial scale. High-current particle beams strike a tritium gas target to produce an intense neutron flux, which SHINE applies across four staged business phases: neutron imaging and radiation-effects testing (the Phoenix Imaging Center, the FLARE 14 MeV radiation-effects service, and a nuclear fuel scanner), medical isotope production (Cassiopeia, which makes the non-carrier-added lutetium-177 product Ilumira, and Chrysalis, a molybdenum-99 facility backed by a conditional $263M U.S. Department of Energy loan), used nuclear fuel recycling (the REDUCE process, with partners including Orano and Deep Isolation), and ultimately fusion energy. SHINE designs and manufactures its own particle accelerators, fusion targets and radiochemical processing systems, and merged with Phoenix LLC in 2022. It is a manufacturer of hardware and radiopharmaceuticals rather than a software company, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Anthro Energy
providers.description: Anthro Energy is a battery materials company based in Alameda, California, developing next-generation electrolyte technology for lithium-ion and next-gen battery cells. Its flagship Proteus platform is a drop-in electrolyte that increases energy density, improves safety, and adds mechanical integrity without requiring changes to existing gigafactory manufacturing infrastructure, and is compatible with a wide range of anodes, separators, and cathodes. Spun out of research at Stanford, Anthro Energy is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and Ultratech Capital. It is a physical-materials company with no public API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and market discovery.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: David Energy
providers.description: David Energy is a clean-energy technology company and licensed electricity retailer that installs free plug-in smart batteries for homes and businesses. Its software charges batteries when grid power is cheap and discharges them during peak-price periods to lower customers' monthly utility bills, alongside bill-monitoring and thermostat-management advisory tools. Backed by Union Square Ventures, David Energy operates in the New York City market with a stated mission of powering the grid on 100% clean energy and shifting the balance of energy control from institutions toward consumers.

providers.name: Thea Energy
providers.description: Thea Energy, Inc. is a fusion energy company headquartered in Kearny, New Jersey, founded in 2022 on stellarator physics and engineering developed at Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. Thea is reinventing the stellarator by replacing complex, hand-wound 3D modular coils with a phased array of simple planar electromagnetic coils, moving the complexity of shaping the magnetic field out of the hardware and into a software control stack that can be tuned over an asset's lifetime. Its first integrated machine, Eos, is a steady-state, neutron-producing stellarator; the follow-on Helios is intended to be an electricity-producing plant. The company raised a $100M Series B in May 2026 led by Thomas Tull's US Innovative Technology Fund, and the U.S. Department of Energy has certified its power plant preconceptual design milestone. Thea publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its only public software surface is a small set of open-source nuclear-engineering and simulation libraries on GitHub.

providers.name: LanzaJet
providers.description: LanzaJet is a sustainable fuels technology company, headquartered at 520 Lake Cook Road, Deerfield, Illinois, that produces and licenses sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. Founded in 2020 as a spin-out of LanzaTech with Suncor and Mitsui, and later backed by Shell, British Airways, Southwest Airlines, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Breakthrough Energy, Groupe ADP, MUFG and All Nippon Airways, the company commercializes a patented Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) process that converts ethanol into synthetic paraffinic kerosene through a continuous catalytic reaction, reaching roughly 90% hydrocarbon selectivity to jet fuel and converting about 98% of the ethanol carbon into salable product. The ATJ pathway was approved by ASTM International in 2018. LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels in Soperton, Georgia — opened in 2024 — is the world's first commercial ethanol-to-jet SAF plant, producing roughly 10 million gallons of SAF and renewable diesel a year, and the company is developing Project Speedbird in the UK alongside a CirculAir joint solution with LanzaTech that widens the feedstock base to municipal solid waste, agricultural residues and industrial off-gases via gas fermentation. LanzaJet sells technology licenses, project development and engineering services and fuel offtake rather than software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and every /.well-known/ discovery probe against its web host returned 404.

providers.name: Resynergi
providers.description: Resynergi is an advanced plastic recycling technology company that builds modular Continuous Microwave Assisted Pyrolysis (CMAP) systems, marketed as AMP Modules, which convert hard-to-recycle waste plastics (HDPE, LDPE, polypropylene and polystyrene) into circular pyrolysis oil (PyOil) and other petrochemical feedstocks. Each 440 sq ft module is designed to process roughly 5 tons of plastic waste per day and produce about 1,000 gallons of PyOil per day, and the company claims a conversion roughly twenty times faster than conventional pyrolysis with a large reduction in CO2-equivalent emissions. Founded in 2015 by Jason Tanne and Brian Bauer around microwave pyrolysis research from the University of Minnesota, Resynergi commercializes its modules in partnership with Lummus Technology, which sells the AMP Modules, and also operates plants near the source of waste under a partner model. This is an industrial process-equipment business; it is not a software vendor and publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AutoGrid
providers.description: AutoGrid Systems is a United States grid-technology company founded in 2011 by Amit Narayan in Redwood City, California, that built AI and machine-learning software for distributed energy resource management (DERMS), virtual power plants, and automated demand response under the AutoGrid Flex platform, selling to investor-owned utilities, retailers, and aggregators rather than to end consumers. It sits on the grid-tech / DERMS layer of the energy value chain - a buyer and orchestrator of utility and device data, not a data custodian - so no Green Button, Consumer Data Right, or smart-meter data-sharing obligation attaches to it. Schneider Electric took control of AutoGrid and then sold it to Uplight in a deal announced 14 December 2023 and closed in early 2024; auto-grid.com now serves only a 270-byte meta-refresh to uplight.com (on an expired TLS certificate as of 27 July 2026) and every developer, docs, api, and data subdomain fails to resolve. Its API posture is therefore honestly none-published - no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, no SDK, no consumer usage API, and no open market data. Its machine-readable contract is instead expressed as protocol conformance, and that is real and still published by the certifying bodies. AutoGrid is a certified OpenADR 2.0a and 2.0b VTN (server) - AutoGrid DROMS and OpenDR Server 2.0, Simple HTTP + XMPP, pull and push - and holds SunSpec Alliance certificate CS-000074 for AutoGrid Flex as an IEEE 2030.5-2018 / CSIP server, tested by Intertek on 12 December 2023 and awarded 22 January 2024. Both surfaces authenticate with mutual TLS x.509 client certificates and were reachable only under commercial contract. The successor surface at docs.uplight.com is real but fully login-gated, redirecting anonymous visitors to a ReadMe dashboard login, and api.uplight.com answers HTTP 401 with "Invalid or no token provided" - partner and customer access only.

providers.name: Gravity
providers.description: Gravity (Gravity Technologies) builds and deploys ultra-fast DC electric-vehicle charging infrastructure for dense urban environments. Its Distributed Energy Access Points (DEAPs) deliver up to five-minute charges from compact, modular hardware that requires minimal real estate and no dedicated utility upgrade, letting operators place high-power charging in garages, curbside, and fleet depots. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time, so this profile captures company identity and the domain security surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: trawa
providers.description: trawa (operated by Future Energy Services GmbH) is a Berlin-based energy management company that helps mid-sized businesses procure and manage electricity. It pairs AI-optimized green-electricity sourcing on the wholesale market with cloud energy-management software that gives customers real-time visibility into consumption, costs, and CO2 emissions, alongside battery storage and smart control of energy-consuming assets such as CHP plants and charging stations. Founded in 2022, trawa is backed by Balderton Capital and Speedinvest. The platform is delivered through a customer web portal and a trust center; no public developer API was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: AGL Resources
providers.description: AGL Resources was an energy services holding company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, whose principal business was the distribution of natural gas to residential, commercial, and industrial customers. In 2016, AGL Resources was acquired by Southern Company and renamed Southern Company Gas, becoming the nation's largest natural gas-only distribution company. The company distributes natural gas through subsidiaries including Atlanta Gas Light, Chattanooga Gas, Nicor Gas, and Virginia Natural Gas. AGL Resources / Southern Company Gas does not offer a public developer API; utility data access is available through third-party data aggregators and community-built integrations.

providers.name: Antora Energy
providers.description: Antora Energy is a San Jose, California clean-energy hardware company founded by Justin Briggs, Andrew Ponec and David Bierman that designs, manufactures and deploys factory-built thermal batteries for heavy industry, data centers and the grid. Antora's system resistively heats blocks of solid carbon to temperatures up to 2,400C when electricity is cheapest, stores that energy for multiple days in a compact modular unit, and discharges it around the clock as radiant heat delivered directly to industrial processes or paired with off-the-shelf steam turbine equipment for firm power; the company also develops thermophotovoltaic (TPV) heat-to-power cells at what it describes as the world's largest TPV manufacturing line. Its HeatCore product delivers heat up to 375C at 300 kW-thermal per module, and its power block is rated at 50 MW-electric. Antora's first giga-scale deployment, Project Big Stone, is a 5 GWh system of more than 200 thermal batteries at POET's bioprocessing plant in Big Stone City, South Dakota, built from empty lot to energy delivery in under twelve months. The company closed a $550 million Series C in 2026. Antora sells energy hardware and long-term energy offtake rather than software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and its only public software surface is Insight, an authenticated steam and power optimization dashboard for named project stakeholders.

providers.name: EcoG
providers.description: EcoG is a Munich-based technology company that builds the software and hardware platform powering electric-vehicle DC fast chargers. Its EcoG OS operating system, Universal Core platform, and controllers let charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), and EV businesses design, launch, and scale DC charging solutions with reduced complexity, claiming more than 15% market share in Europe with operations across India and North America. For developers, EcoG OS exposes an on-device programmatic surface (an OpenAPI-based application interface, a local web interface, and the LifeC remote management tool) so smart value-added charging applications can be built and run at the device level. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from EcoG's public website; it publishes no public REST API developer portal or specification.

providers.name: Exowatt
providers.description: Exowatt is a clean-energy technology company redefining power generation for the AI era. Its flagship Exowatt P3 is a modular, dispatchable solar-thermal energy platform that captures solar energy with proprietary Fresnel lenses and heat exchangers, stores it in a high-efficiency heat battery, and dispatches electricity on demand via a proprietary heat engine, delivering up to 24 hours of dispatchable baseload power. The systems are factory-built in the USA from abundant, low-cost materials without rare-earth minerals, and are aimed at energy-intensive customers such as AI data centers and utilities. Backed by a16z and Felicis, Exowatt is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: General Matter
providers.description: General Matter is a domestic nuclear-fuel company founded in 2024 and based in California, building United States uranium enrichment capacity to produce low-enriched uranium (LEU) and high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for advanced commercial and government nuclear reactors. Co-founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson and backed by Founders Fund, the company was awarded a $900M Department of Energy IDIQ contract and plans a $1.5B commercial enrichment facility at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Kentucky, plus a lease on the Hanford Fuels and Materials Examination Facility in Washington. Its mission is to reduce American reliance on foreign nuclear fuel and strengthen energy independence. General Matter is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heron Power
providers.description: Heron Power is an industrial power-electronics company modernizing the electrical grid with solid-state transformers and integrated power conversion systems. Founded by former Tesla executive Drew Baglino, the company builds Heron Link products that combine a solid-state transformer with a power supply or inverter for two markets: data centers (AI and hyperscale power delivery, including 800 VDC datacenter architectures) and solar-and-storage renewable energy systems. Heron Power targets the grid infrastructure bottlenecks of the clean-energy transition, replacing century-old passive transformer technology with dense, controllable, software-defined power hardware. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Breakthrough Energy. Heron Power is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: Marvel Fusion
providers.description: Marvel Fusion is a Munich-based deep-tech company founded in 2019 that is developing laser-based inertial confinement fusion energy. It combines a proprietary fast-ignition approach with innovations across lasers, fuel targets, and power-plant design to make commercial fusion power viable, building on the National Ignition Facility 2022 ignition breakthrough. The company operates in Germany and the United States, with a demonstration facility in Fort Collins, Colorado, and has raised over $400M from venture capital, industrial partners, and public funding. As a physics and energy-infrastructure company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web/domain security posture.

providers.name: Proxima Fusion
providers.description: Proxima Fusion is a Munich-based fusion energy company building the first generation of commercial fusion power plants using quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarators. Spun out of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, the company is developing Stellaris, a stellarator power plant concept, with milestones that include a Stellarator Model Coil and an Alpha demonstration stellarator on the path to grid-scale fusion energy. Proxima Fusion is a privately held deep-tech startup and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: rabot.energy
providers.description: rabot.energy (RABOT Energy DE GmbH) is a Hamburg-based German electricity supplier offering dynamic and fixed-rate power tariffs where consumers pay hourly rates that track the wholesale electricity market. The company provides 100% renewable energy certified by TÜV NORD, smart meter installation and management, EV charging optimization (Autostrom), and home battery storage (Rabot Flow), all managed through a consumer mobile app for consumption monitoring. It is a consumer-facing energy retailer; no public developer portal or API is currently published. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital.

providers.name: Cormint
providers.description: Cormint Data Systems, Inc. is a Texas-based, vertically integrated developer and operator of power infrastructure for large-scale data centers and compute. The company designs, manufactures, deploys and operates its own electrical and site infrastructure in-house — from PDU wiring and PLC controls through transformer integration and substation work — and runs 130 MW energized today at its Fort Blocks site near Fort Stockton in West Texas, with a second 58 MW site (Bobcat) under construction near Orange Grove in ERCOT Load Zone South and a stated pipeline of roughly 370 MW across 707 controlled acres. Cormint built the operating platform in bitcoin mining, where it reports power costs of 2.3–3.1 cents per kWh and a #1 peer ranking on cost efficiency, and is now positioning the same platform for AI and HPC workloads as a colocation and EPC-style infrastructure owner-operator. It is an energy and data-center infrastructure business rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Plains All American Pipeline
providers.description: Plains All American Pipeline is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Plains All American Pipeline API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Portland General Electric
providers.description: Portland General Electric is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Portland General Electric API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: South Jersey Industries
providers.description: South Jersey Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The South Jersey Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Sunoco LP
providers.description: Sunoco LP (NYSE: SUN) is a master limited partnership and the premier independent fuel distributor in the United States, distributing over 15 billion gallons of fuel annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations and operating more than 160 terminals. Sunoco LP is affiliated with Energy Transfer (parent of Sunoco GP, the general partner). On November 3, 2025 Sunoco closed its $9.1 billion acquisition of Parkland Corporation (announced May 5, 2025), creating SunocoCorp LLC, which began trading on the NYSE under ticker "SUNC". The Parkland acquisition substantially expands Sunoco's footprint into Canada and additional international markets, adding Parkland's refining, retail, and commercial fuels businesses to Sunoco's North American distribution network.

providers.name: Syzygy Plasmonics
providers.description: Syzygy Plasmonics is a Houston, Texas deep-decarbonization company commercializing photocatalytic chemical manufacturing. Its Rigel reactor cell uses photonic energy from renewable electricity in place of combustion heat to drive reforming reactions, and its NovaSAF / GHG e-Reforming pathway converts waste biogas into low-carbon sustainable aviation fuel, independently assessed as eligible for both ISCC EU RFNBO and Advanced BioSAF certification. Adjacent targets include hydrogen from ammonia e-cracking, syngas, methanol, butadiene and other commodity chemicals, sold as reactor hardware plus a licensing and front-end engineering support package. Syzygy is a hardware and process-licensing business, not a software vendor: as of 2026-08-29 it publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: 1001 AI
providers.description: 1001 (also known as 1001 AI) is a deeptech artificial intelligence company founded in 2025 by Bilal Abu-Ghazaleh, a former director of generative AI operations at Scale AI, and headquartered between London and Dubai. The company builds sovereign AI operating systems for critical infrastructure — live operational models that help operators across aviation and airports, ports and logistics, energy and grids, construction, and manufacturing predict issues, automate and optimize decisions, and improve operational efficiency, while retaining full local ownership and governance of their AI systems. Focused primarily on the GCC and wider MENA region, 1001 raised a $9 million seed round in October 2025 led by CIV, General Catalyst, and Lux Capital, followed by a $30 million Series A in June 2026 led by Lux Capital with Sanabil Investments, 9Yards, and Hanabi joining and existing backers General Catalyst, CIV, and Stanford AI researcher Chris Ré increasing their commitments. As of this profile, 1001 publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK; this entry captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Condor Energy
providers.description: Condor Energy is an AI-powered energy management operating system for enterprise energy procurement, built for industrial companies, retailers, and data center operators who buy electricity at scale. The platform aggregates consumption data, PPAs, solar, batteries, and live market data into real-time dashboards; models load against market dynamics to execute hedging strategies and produce board-ready price-risk reporting; and analyzes granular load data to find flexibility opportunities and evaluate ROI on solar, battery, EV-charging, and hybrid investments. Founded in 2026 by former electricity traders and energy physicists, the Paris-based company is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Noteworthy AI
providers.description: Noteworthy AI is a Techstars-backed company delivering AI-powered grid inspection for electric utilities. Its Noteworthy Inspect product mounts smart cameras on utility fleet vehicles and applies computer-vision and machine-learning analytics to automatically identify pole defects, inventory grid components, and assess distribution-infrastructure conditions during routine operations, without dedicated inspection crews. Use cases span asset inventory and inspection, lighting audits, storm-damage assessment, vegetation management, and joint-use equipment tracking, helping utilities cut inspection operating costs while improving grid reliability and safety. Customers include FirstEnergy, NextEra Energy, Exelon, Xcel Energy, Alabama Power, and Georgia Power; technology partners include NVIDIA, Dell Technologies, Esri, and EPRI. Noteworthy AI is SOC 2 Type II compliant. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Amentum
providers.description: Amentum Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: AMTM) is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions company serving U.S. federal customers across defense, intelligence, energy, space, and civilian missions, with allied work in the United Kingdom and Australia. The company was created from the spin-off of AECOM's Management Services business in 2020, and on September 27, 2024 completed a Reverse Morris Trust transaction with Jacobs Solutions to merge Jacobs' Critical Mission Solutions (CMS) and Cyber & Intelligence (C&I) businesses into Amentum. Post-merger Amentum reports approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenue, a $47.1 billion backlog, ~53,000 employees in 80 countries, and is headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia. The business is organized around six capability areas — Mission Modernization & Sustainment, Space Systems, Digital Transformation, Sustainability & Environment, Advanced Energy Solutions, and Data Analytics & Cyber. Most delivery occurs under contract through classified, CAC-gated, or program portals; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or REST API has been identified.

providers.name: Nanotech Energy
providers.description: Nanotech Energy is an advanced materials manufacturer that develops and produces graphene-based super materials and the energy-storage products built from them. Its catalog spans graphene powders, graphene oxide pastes, dispersions, conductive inks and conductive adhesives, silver nanowires, and non-flammable lithium-ion battery cells and packs aimed at home and grid energy storage, marine, household and electric-vehicle applications. The company also offers customer-facing testing, analysis and product development services to help customers scale a graphene formulation from concept to full production. It is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes a marketing and product website but no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Volter
providers.description: Volter (Get Volter Ltd) is a London-based energy platform that connects UK businesses with renewable generators to procure cheaper, greener electricity, and helps commercial real estate owners and generators deploy, optimize, and monetize rooftop solar and other onsite renewable assets. The platform spans renewable energy matching, solar optimization, and a forthcoming energy management suite with analytics, anomaly detection, flexible asset control, and battery storage. Backed by Transition and Seedcamp with a $3.2M pre-seed round in 2024. Volter does not currently publish a public API or developer documentation.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (originally launched as Tesseract) is a UK-based, vertically integrated energy supplier founded by former Revolut executives Alan Chang and Charles Orr. It buys power from generators and supplies gas and electricity directly to residential and business customers, positioning itself to beat the UK price cap with variable, fixed and multi-rate tariffs, 30-minute billing updates, EV charging, solar/battery export tracking and an in-app AI assistant called "Plugs." The company raised $78M led by Balderton Capital and Lakestar. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Fuse Energy publishes only a consumer-facing web and mobile app and no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Indian Energy Exchange
providers.description: Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) is India's largest electricity trading platform, operating a nationwide automated exchange for the physical delivery of electricity, renewable energy, and certificates. IEX runs Day-Ahead, Real-Time, Term-Ahead, Renewable Energy Certificate and Energy Saving Certificate market segments, matching buy and sell bids across a member network of distribution utilities, industrial and commercial consumers, and power generators. For members with sophisticated trading needs IEX offers a members-only trading API (currently for the iDAM and RTM segments) supporting order placement, trade-data retrieval and real-time monitoring for automated and high-frequency trading; access is provisioned to registered members rather than published as a public developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: USA Rare Earth
providers.description: USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) is an American critical-minerals and advanced-materials company building a domestic mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain. It operates a 310,000 sq. ft. sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma, and holds the Round Top heavy rare earth and critical minerals deposit in Hudspeth County, West Texas. The company produces rare earth elements, oxides, metals and sintered permanent magnets for defense, automotive, robotics, industrial and clean-energy customers, with the stated aim of reducing U.S. dependence on offshore rare earth processing and magnet production. It is a materials producer and manufacturer, not a software or data company, and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: ecoplanet
providers.description: ecoplanet provides cloud-based, integrated energy management software for German mid-market companies. The platform combines three core functions: real-time consumption monitoring through meter integration with AI-powered anomaly detection and automated load-shifting on price signals; strategic energy procurement using algorithmic purchasing across spot markets, tranches, and power purchase agreements (PPAs); and automated ISO 50001 compliance documentation. The company reports customers achieve up to 15% consumption savings and ~13.9% average price advantages on energy purchases. Backed by EQT Ventures and HV Capital. No public developer/API surface was found at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Swell Energy
providers.description: Swell Energy is a residential clean-energy company that designs, finances, installs, and operates home solar, battery storage, and virtual power plant (VPP) systems for homeowners, businesses, and utilities. Its Swell Compass platform connects to home energy devices to monitor, report, and optimize energy use, and coordinates aggregated distributed batteries into grid services (GridRevenue programs) in partnership with utilities. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a consumer web and mobile experience (Compass) rather than a public developer API; no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Tesoro
providers.description: Tesoro Corporation (later rebranded as Andeavor) was a Fortune 100 independent petroleum refiner and marketer headquartered in San Antonio, Texas. Founded in 1968, the company operated ten refineries in the Western United States with combined crude oil capacity of approximately 1.2 million barrels per day and approximately 3,000 branded retail gas stations. Tesoro rebranded as Andeavor in 2017 following its acquisition of Western Refining, and was acquired by Marathon Petroleum on October 1, 2018. No public developer API was offered.

providers.name: BP
providers.description: BP (British Petroleum) is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, operating in over 70 countries across oil and gas exploration, production, refining, distribution, marketing, petrochemicals, power generation, and renewable energy. BP operates an API Marketplace developer portal (developer.bp.com) enabling seamless integration with BP's digital services, providing API discovery, testing playgrounds, documentation, and billing management for energy sector integrations.

providers.name: SCANA Corporation
providers.description: SCANA Corporation was an American regulated electric and natural gas public utility headquartered in Cayce, South Carolina. Its primary subsidiaries included South Carolina Electric & Gas (SCE&G), which provided electric and natural gas service to approximately 660,000 electric customers in South Carolina, and PSNC Energy, which served over one million natural gas customers in North Carolina and Georgia. SCANA was acquired by Dominion Energy in January 2019, after which the SCANA, SCE&G, and PSNC names were retired and operations were integrated into Dominion Energy's Southeast Energy Group. SCANA Energy Natural Gas continues to operate as a retail natural gas marketer in Georgia.

providers.name: United Refining Company
providers.description: United Refining Company is an independent, integrated petroleum company headquartered in Warren, Pennsylvania. The company owns and operates a petroleum refinery and a network of retail gasoline stations and convenience stores under the Kwik Fill and Country Fair brands in the northeastern United States. United Refining does not offer publicly documented APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Equilibrium Energy
providers.description: Equilibrium Energy is a venture-backed clean energy technology company building PowerOS, an agentic AI platform for the power and energy sector. The platform is designed to solve the extreme data and systems fragmentation across the power tech stack, uniting enterprise data, models, and systems under a common ontology and code frameworks so that power companies can deploy power-specific AI with guardrails they control. PowerOS bundles enterprise agents (trader and research copilots, app co-developers, data ingestion and transformation), configurable application suites (portfolio management, portfolio construction, development workbenches, middle and back office), and reusable core services (optimization, forecasting, risk, grid and market fundamentals, trading). The company's Mission Control product is in invite-only beta. Equilibrium Energy is backed by DCVC and is headquartered in the United States. It currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, news, and organization surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Stegra
providers.description: Stegra (formerly H2 Green Steel) is a Stockholm-headquartered industrial company, founded in 2020 and backed by Vargas Holding, building what it describes as Europe's first large-scale near-zero-emission steel plant in Boden, northern Sweden. The 270-hectare Boden site integrates a giga-scale electrolyzer producing green hydrogen from renewable Nordic electricity, a direct-reduction plant making green iron without coking coal, and a downstream steel mill — a combination Stegra says cuts steelmaking emissions by roughly 95 percent versus the blast-furnace route. Its commercial products are green steel, green iron and green hydrogen, sold to automotive, construction and appliance customers. Stegra is a heavy-industry manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it operates no public developer portal, publishes no API documentation, and serves no machine-readable API contract. Its only public engineering surface is the stegraab GitHub organization, which maintains community Terraform providers and a tflint ruleset used for its own internal infrastructure.

providers.name: Terawatt Infrastructure
providers.description: Terawatt Infrastructure is a US infrastructure company that acquires, develops, owns, and operates purpose-built electric-vehicle charging centers for commercial fleets — medium- and heavy-duty trucking, drayage, autonomous vehicle and rideshare operators. The company sells charging-as-a-service rather than software: it holds real estate and grid interconnection, builds high-power charging sites (including the I-10 electrified corridor and sites near the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach), and runs them with its own proprietary Charge Management Software, operations and maintenance program, and a customer reservations portal. Terawatt states publicly that it has implemented the Open Charge Point Interface (OCPI) with custom extensions so fleet customers get visibility into its charging facilities, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract for that surface.

providers.name: Verdagy
providers.description: Verdagy is a Moss Landing, California clean-energy hardware company that designs and manufactures dynamic alkaline water electrolysis systems for large-scale green hydrogen production. Its eDynamic platform runs very large-area membrane-based electrochemical cells at high current density with dynamic turndown, so electrolyzers can follow intermittent renewable power, targeting fossil-fuel cost parity for clean hydrogen by 2028 without subsidies. The company operates a 2 MW eDynamic demonstration plant at Moss Landing with more than 21,000 commercial cell hours, plus 500 kW and 100 kW test plants, and opened a DOE-supported gigawatt-scale manufacturing facility of more than 100,000 square feet in Newark, California. Verdagy sells electrolyzer hardware and project capacity to industrial hydrogen buyers — refining, ammonia, methanol, e-fuels and SAF — rather than software; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: I-Pulse
providers.description: I-Pulse Inc. is a U.S.-based industrial technology company founded in 2007 by Robert Friedland and Laurent Frescaline that commercializes High Pulsed Power (HPP) — releasing very short, extremely high-power electrical discharges from small amounts of stored energy to generate magnetic forces, shockwaves, electrical arcs and electric fields. I-Pulse holds 55 patents licensed exclusively to its operating businesses across natural-resource transformation (I-ROX rock comminution, I-Mine, iTerra non-chemical weed control, IPW), the energy transition (G-Pulse pulsed-power geothermal drilling, Blue Spark Geothermal), manufacturing (Bmax electromagnetic metal forming and welding, CSI Technologies high-energy capacitors) and R&D (I-Cube, Typhoon). It operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico and Toulouse, France, with offices in Canada, the UK and Singapore, and signed a $250 million CHIPS R&D award with the U.S. Department of Commerce in 2026 for semiconductor and pulsed-power development. I-Pulse is a hardware and industrial-process company; it publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Project Canary
providers.description: Project Canary is a Denver-based climate technology company that helps oil and gas operators and natural gas utilities turn methane emissions data into operational intelligence. Founded in 2019, its Canary SENSE platform unifies measurement data from sensors, satellites, aircraft, SCADA, and field teams into a single view that drives decisions, reduces costs, and supports regulatory reporting (OGMP 2.0 and other frameworks). The company builds high-precision methane detection hardware (Canary RECON, Aeris PICO) and a proprietary predictive emissions model (methaneML) trained on a multi-year, high-fidelity methane dataset, serving upstream and midstream operators as well as gas distribution utilities across the United States. Project Canary has raised $121M (Series B) and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and Techstars. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI is published at this time; this profile captures identity, a verbatim llms.txt, and security posture.

providers.name: Sealed
providers.description: Sealed is a New York-based climate technology company, founded in 2012, whose Sealed Pro platform helps home-improvement contractors sell and finance home weatherization and electrification projects — insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, smart thermostats and heat-pump water heaters. Sealed pairs energy data and analytics with a rebate and incentive engine that qualifies a project at the point of sale, guarantees a minimum rebate amount, files the utility and Inflation Reduction Act (HOMES / HEAR) paperwork on the contractor's behalf, and pays the contractor after installation while Sealed carries the incentive-collection risk. The company began as a direct-to-consumer home energy retrofit provider with the first residential energy-savings guarantee, and relaunched as Sealed Pro, a contractor-facing software platform, working with utilities and state energy offices on measured- and modeled-savings programs.

providers.name: Regency Energy Partners
providers.description: Regency Energy Partners LP (NYSE: RGP) was a publicly traded master limited partnership focused on midstream natural gas services including gathering, processing, contract compression, treating, and transportation of natural gas, crude oil, and natural gas liquids. Regency operated in North Louisiana, West Texas, and the Mid-Continent region before being acquired by Energy Transfer Partners in a $11 billion transaction in 2015 and merged into Energy Transfer's broader midstream operations.

providers.name: Airforestry
providers.description: AirForestry is a Swedish climate-technology company developing autonomous electric drones that perform forest thinning from the air. Its system pairs AI and computer vision for tree identification and selection with a lightweight aerial harvesting tool, letting a fleet of drones fell and extract trees without ground machinery. The result is forestry with zero soil compaction, no root damage and no machine tracks, higher operational efficiency, and lower emissions than conventional harvesters, while increasing forest growth and carbon sequestration. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: DNOW
providers.description: DNOW Inc. (NYSE: DNOW), formerly NOW Inc. and operating as DistributionNOW, is a Houston-headquartered Fortune 1000 distributor of pipe, valves, fittings (PVF), pumps and packaged, engineered process and production equipment serving the upstream, midstream, downstream energy, and industrial sectors. Spun off from National Oilwell Varco in 2014 and built on a heritage that spans more than 160 years, DNOW combines a global network of distribution branches and engineering facilities with the DigitalNOW platform — shop.dnow.com B2B eCommerce, cXML/OCI ERP punchout integrations, the eSpec product configurator, the AccessNOW automated inventory control system, and a library of customer-facing mobile applications. DNOW does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, or a self-serve API program; customer integrations are delivered through configured cXML/OCI punchout sessions tied to enterprise ERP systems. In June 2025 DNOW announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire MRC Global in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $1.5 billion.

providers.name: Powerledger
providers.description: Powerledger (Powerledger AG / Power Ledger Pty Ltd, Perth, Western Australia) builds software for tracking, tracing and trading renewable energy and environmental commodities. Its platform is modular and sold to utilities, retailers, network operators, generators and corporates rather than to developers: xGrid and uGrid for peer-to-peer energy trading across and behind the meter, TraceX as a marketplace for Renewable Energy Certificates and other Energy Attribute Certificates (integrated with the M-RETS and ERCOT registries), Vision and PPA Vision for 24/7 renewable portfolio and PPA tracking, plus hydrogen and EV settlement products. Powerledger originally ran its own permissioned Solana-derived chain (the Powerledger Energy Blockchain, source at github.com/PowerLedger/powr) and has since moved to Solana mainnet, where the POWR SPL token lives. As of this profile Powerledger publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: WPX Energy
providers.description: WPX Energy was an independent oil and gas exploration and production company focused on the Permian and Williston basins. In 2021, WPX Energy completed a merger with Devon Energy Corporation to form one of the largest independent oil and gas producers in the United States. As a result of the merger, WPX Energy no longer operates as a standalone company and does not maintain a public developer API. WPX Energy data is available through financial data providers such as Intrinio and through Devon Energy's current platforms.

providers.name: Wunder
providers.description: Wunder (formerly Wunder Capital, wewunder.com, now wunderpower.com) is a commercial clean-energy company that deploys solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure across real estate portfolios with no-CapEx energy solutions, managing projects from design through operations in 40+ US states. Backed by Techstars and a $650M partnership with Blackstone, Wunder runs its project development on Astra, a proprietary internal platform for energy data analysis, forecasting, and automation. Wunder publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Coterra Energy
providers.description: Coterra Energy is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Coterra Energy API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: CrossAmerica Partners
providers.description: CrossAmerica Partners is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CrossAmerica Partners API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: SunEdison
providers.description: SunEdison was a renewable energy company that developed, financed, installed, owned, and operated solar power plants and wind energy plants globally. Originally founded as MEMC Electronic Materials in 1959, SunEdison became the world's leading renewable energy developer before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2016 and emerging as a restructured private company in 2017. No public developer API was documented.

providers.name: Whiting Petroleum
providers.description: Whiting Petroleum was an independent oil and gas company engaged in the exploration, development, and production of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids primarily in the Williston Basin (Bakken Shale) in North Dakota and Montana. In July 2022, Whiting Petroleum merged with Oasis Petroleum to form Chord Energy Corporation, which trades on NASDAQ under the ticker symbol CHRD.

providers.name: Beacon Power Services
providers.description: Beacon Power Services (BPS) is an African energy-technology company building software that helps electricity utilities and energy consumers manage the power grid more efficiently. Its platform spans three products: CAIMS, a customer and asset information management system for utility network, survey, installation, and new-service-connection management; Adora, a grid network management solution for commercial operations, network management, and field operations that helps utilities optimize operations and increase profitability; and Xepp, a consumer mobile app for energy consumption monitoring, instant electricity top-up, solar integration, and flexible payments. BPS serves utilities and distribution companies across Africa (clients include ECG and AEDC) and is backed by Partech. This profile currently has no public API or developer surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: enechain
providers.description: enechain operates the largest energy exchange in Japan, offering trading opportunities for wholesale electricity and environmental values across an over-the-counter marketplace that connects energy market participants. Headquartered in Tokyo, the company builds energy markets that help buyers and sellers discover prices, manage risk, and trade power and environmental-value products, under the mission "Building Energy Markets, Coloring Our Society." enechain was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Excelergy
providers.description: Excelergy is a global provider of high-performance retail energy billing and revenue management software, now part of Harris Computer. Its flagship product, RevenueManager, is a cloud-based, meter-to-cash billing platform used by competitive energy retailers across more than 200 jurisdictions in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. RevenueManager handles residential, commercial, industrial, and wholesale billing across multiple commodities (electricity, natural gas, water, heat, and sewage), supporting complex tariff and pricing models, customer lifecycle management, smart-meter and time-of-use pricing, and built-in Salesforce CRM integration. The platform exposes APIs for connectivity with third-party systems and access to data held in the RevenueManager database. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; Excelergy publishes a corporate marketing site and a customer support portal but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Tantalus
providers.description: Tantalus Systems (TSX: GRID; OTCQX: TGMPF) is a technology company that has served public power utilities and electric cooperatives for over 35 years, modernizing electrical distribution grids through data-centric solutions. Its Tantalus Grid Modernization Platform (TGMP) unifies intelligence across the distribution grid, connecting metering, load and DER management, grid automation, and data management across both legacy and modern infrastructure. Product lines include TRUConnect advanced metering infrastructure (AMI), TRUFlex load and DER management, TRUGrid automation analytics, TRUSync grid data management, and the TRUSense behind-the-meter gateway. Tantalus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; integration with back-end utility software is delivered through standard data formats and handled via its technical support and integration teams.

providers.name: Jimmy
providers.description: Jimmy (Jimmy Energy SAS) is a French nuclear-technology company, founded in 2020 as a spin-off from the CEA, that designs, builds and operates small modular high-temperature reactors it calls thermal generators — helium-cooled HTR units the company describes as bus-sized — to deliver carbon-free process heat directly to industrial sites under secured 20-year supply-and-price contracts. Jimmy is headquartered in Paris with an industrial platform at Le Creusot in Burgundy, targets food, paper, sugar and chemicals producers that currently burn natural gas for process heat, and filed the first SMR creation-authorization request in France for a generator at the Cristanol site in Bazancourt. Jimmy sells heat, not software: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification, and this profile records that measured absence rather than assuming it.

providers.name: XFuel
providers.description: XFuel develops, patents, and deploys technologies that transform diverse waste into low-carbon drop-in transport fuels, using its Chemical Liquid Refining (CLR) and Mechanical Carbon Conversion (MECC) processes to produce marine (ISO 8217 DMA), road (EN590), and in-development sustainable aviation fuels. Headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, with operations in Bunyola, Spain, and backed by Union Square Ventures. XFuel publishes no public API or developer program as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: 280 Earth
providers.description: 280 Earth is a direct air capture (DAC) company that permanently removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Originally launched in 2018 inside X, the Alphabet moonshot factory, and spun out as an independent company in 2022, it is backed by Sergey Brin, Builders VC and a $50M Series B. Its proprietary sorbent moves through a gravity-fed dual-chamber system that continuously cycles material between capturing and releasing CO2, running on low-grade industrial waste heat or clean electricity and producing fresh water as a byproduct. Its first pilot plant, in The Dalles, Oregon, captures 500 tons of CO2 per year on a site sized for more than 20,000 tons per year at full build-out, and underpins a $40M offtake agreement with the Frontier carbon removal buyer consortium (Google, Meta, Stripe, Shopify and others). 280 Earth is a hardware and carbon-removal operator; as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer surface, API, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Blixt
providers.description: BL!XT (Blixt) is a Swedish deep-tech company building intelligent, programmable power infrastructure that turns electrical distribution from analog systems into digitally controlled, software-defined platforms. Its products include ZERO, a solid-state current-control switchgear for circuit-level protection, monitoring, and automation; X-VERTER, a software-defined voltage conversion system with integrated energy storage; and THE ZONE, an AI-driven software intelligence layer that coordinates connected distribution devices for real-time analysis, failure prediction, and load balancing. BL!XT serves data centers, industrial manufacturing, maritime vessels, grid providers, and defense. Headquartered in Kista, Sweden and backed by Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: NEO TECH MOBILITY HOLDINGS LIMITED
providers.description: NEO TECH MOBILITY HOLDINGS LIMITED (Neo Mobility) is a UAE-based B2B electric-mobility startup driving sustainable transportation across the MENA region. Neo bundles electric-vehicle fleets, charging infrastructure, an integrated fleet/driver/operations/energy management platform, driver-safety programs, and human-capital support into a single subscription-based ecosystem — delivering EV Delivery-as-a-Service for e-commerce, food delivery, and last-mile logistics, alongside e-taxi mobility. The company publishes no public developer or API program; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: ConocoPhillips
providers.description: ConocoPhillips is a leading global exploration and production company, headquartered in Houston, Texas, that is uniquely equipped to deliver reliable, responsibly produced oil and natural gas. The company operates in more than a dozen countries with conventional and unconventional crude oil, natural gas, LNG, and natural gas liquids assets. ConocoPhillips does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations portal, a vendor relations portal (powered by third-party platforms such as GEP and Taulia), an LNG technology and licensing program, and a custom sustainability report builder.

providers.name: Westar Energy
providers.description: Westar Energy was the largest electric utility in Kansas, providing electric service to homes, businesses, and industries throughout Kansas before merging with Great Plains Energy in 2018 to form Evergy, Inc. As Evergy, the company continues to serve approximately 1.6 million customers in Kansas and Missouri with a focus on grid modernization, smart metering (AMI) through its Gridstream Connect IoT platform, and clean energy transformation including wind power and demand response programs.

providers.name: Zanskar
providers.description: Zanskar (Zanskar Geothermal & Minerals, Inc.) is a Salt Lake City-based geothermal energy company founded in 2021 by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards. It uses custom artificial intelligence, machine learning, and subsurface geoscience to discover and develop conventional geothermal resources, with a mission to make geothermal the most affordable form of widely-deployable, 24/7 carbon-free power. The company raised a $115M Series C and is backed by Obvious Ventures and Union Square Ventures. Zanskar publishes public geothermal datasets on the Snowflake Marketplace; it does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Dynegy
providers.description: Dynegy is a retail electric service provider and part of the Vistra Corp family of companies, delivering simple, price-protected retail electricity plans for homes and businesses across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Midwest, including Ohio, Illinois, and Pennsylvania. No public APIs have been documented for Dynegy.

providers.name: CHINT
providers.description: CHINT (Chint Group) is a global smart-energy and intelligent-electrical solutions provider founded in 1984 and headquartered in Wenzhou, China, with operations across more than 140 countries. Its portfolio spans low-voltage electrical equipment (IEC and UL), power transmission and distribution systems, switchgear, instruments and meters, EV charging, and clean-energy systems including solar PV and battery storage, serving power utilities, buildings, telecom and data centers, industrial, and OEM sectors. CHINT does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity and its public web properties. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan / former Sequoia China).

providers.name: CleanCapital
providers.description: CleanCapital is a New York based clean energy investment firm, founded in 2015, that develops, constructs, acquires, owns and operates distributed-generation solar and energy storage projects across the United States. It concentrates on the commercial and municipal middle market between residential rooftop and utility-scale generation, selling power to businesses, schools, nonprofits, municipalities and community solar subscribers, and it buys operating and late-stage development projects from developers through a dedicated project-acquisition practice. The firm reports more than $1.5 billion of capital deployed, 450+ MW under management, 235 MW developed and constructed, 200+ energy customers and over 1,000 GWh of emissions-free generation, backed by institutional partners including Manulife Investment Management / John Hancock, BlackRock and CarVal Investors. CleanCapital is an asset owner and investment manager rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its customer portal at app.cleancapital.com now redirects to the third-party Dock Energy platform.

providers.name: ECO2GROW
providers.description: ECO2GROW is a German renewable-energy procurement company serving mid-sized businesses. It builds an individually optimized electricity procurement mix that combines Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) sourced directly from German solar and wind farms with spot-market and forward contracts, giving companies enterprise-level pricing, long-term fixed rates, and traceable green power. The service automates the optimization of a company's procurement strategy and reduces the complexity and transaction costs of closing a PPA, helping industrial and mid-market buyers lower CO2 emissions through verifiable renewable sourcing. ECO2GROW is a Techstars portfolio company. As a B2B energy procurement and advisory business it operates a marketing/consulting web presence and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Greenlyte
providers.description: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies is an Essen, Germany based climate-tech company building its LiquidSolar platform, which liquefies air, sun, and water into 99% pure carbon and hydrogen feedstocks to produce synthetic e-fuels (sustainable aviation fuel, synthetic methanol, and synthetic natural gas) for hard-to-decarbonize industries. Founded as a direct air capture and power-to-liquid venture, Greenlyte has raised more than 55M EUR from Carbon Removal Partners, Earlybird, Partech, AENU, and Green Generation Fund. It was surfaced through VC portfolio mining and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Greenlyte publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Realta Fusion
providers.description: Realta Fusion is a fusion-energy company developing compact, scalable, modular magnetic-mirror fusion systems branded CoSMo fusion to deliver zero-carbon heat and electricity for industrial energy needs. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company designs prefabricated fusion modules that can be assembled to meet a variety of industrial power and process-heat requirements, targeting decarbonization of the roughly 37 billion metric tons of annual CO2 emissions from energy production. Realta Fusion is a hardware and energy-systems company and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks it in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Delek US
providers.description: Delek US is an alias for Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK), a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. The canonical profile for this company is maintained under aid delek-us-holdings; this entry exists as a name alias and references the corporate site. Delek does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

providers.name: Range Resources
providers.description: Range Resources is an independent natural gas, natural gas liquids, and oil company engaged in the exploration, development, and acquisition of natural gas and oil properties primarily in the Appalachian region. Range does not publish a public developer API; this index tracks the company's public-facing digital properties for reference.

providers.name: Cameron International
providers.description: Cameron International (formerly Cooper Cameron Corporation) was a leading provider of flow equipment products, systems, and services to the worldwide oil, gas, and process industries. In 2016 the business was acquired by Schlumberger (now SLB) and its pressure-control, drilling, subsea, valves, measurement, and compression product lines were integrated into SLB's digital oilfield portfolio. Cameron-branded capabilities are now delivered and integrated through the SLB DELFI digital platform and its developer APIs rather than through a standalone Cameron developer program.

providers.name: Archimetis
providers.description: Archimetis builds an AI-powered Operational Reasoning System for refineries, chemicals, and heavy process industries. The platform unifies data from disparate operational sources — plant historians, linear programs, advanced process control models, and digital engineering documents — into a single intelligence layer, then continuously monitors operations, performs complex engineering analysis, and applies industry best practices to surface actionable insights for operators and engineers. Marketed as "See more. Solve smarter," it targets margin improvement, cost savings, and process safety across refining, chemicals, and other heavy industries. Founded in 2023, the company raised $11.5M led by Inspired Capital. Archimetis is an enterprise B2B platform engaged through guided working sessions and demos; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Buckeye Partners
providers.description: Buckeye Partners, LP is a master limited partnership that owns and operates one of the largest independent liquid petroleum product pipeline and terminal systems in the United States. Buckeye transports and stores refined petroleum products including gasoline, jet fuel, diesel, and heating oil, connecting refineries and import terminals to local distribution markets across the Eastern US, Midwest, and internationally. Buckeye was taken private by IFM Investors in 2019.

providers.name: CHS Inc.
providers.description: CHS Inc. is a Fortune 500 diversified, integrated, global agricultural cooperative owned by farmers, ranchers, cooperatives, and individual producers. Headquartered in Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota, CHS describes itself as the largest farmer-owned cooperative in the United States, with more than 750 member cooperatives, 75,000+ individual producer-owners, and 20,000+ preferred stockholders. The cooperative serves customers in 65 countries through three primary business divisions: Agriculture (crop nutrients, crop protection, precision agriculture, seed, animal nutrition, and oilseed products), Energy (refined fuels, propane, lubricants, pipelines, terminals, and renewable fuels under the Cenex brand), and Services (hedging, payment solutions, transportation, and capital services). Major brands include Cenex, Allegiant (seed), Payback (animal nutrition), and N-Edge (crop nutrients). CHS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are provided through digital platforms such as MyCHS (online portal for grain tickets, billing, and payments) and CHS Connect (digital self-service for crop protection and energy wholesale customers).

providers.name: Exelon
providers.description: Exelon Corporation is one of the largest energy delivery companies in the United States, serving more than 10 million customers through its regulated electric and gas utility subsidiaries: Atlantic City Electric, BGE, ComEd, Delmarva Power, PECO, and Pepco. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, Exelon operates across multiple U.S. states. No public consumer-facing developer APIs have been identified for Exelon; customer self-service is conducted through utility portals.

providers.name: Hades
providers.description: Hades Mining GmbH is a Munich-based deep-tech extraction company building technology-first methods for accessing critical minerals and geothermal energy from ultra-deep rock formations. Its flagship system, Cerberus, uses high-power continuous-wave fiber lasers delivered through proprietary fiber optics to fracture rock without mechanical bit wear, paired with in-situ recovery (ISR) fluid circulation to extract minerals without open-pit excavation. The company positions itself at the intersection of geology, engineering, and geopolitics under the tagline "Sovereignty begins subsurface," aiming to reduce Western dependence on imported critical minerals. Hades is backed by HV Capital and Headline via a EUR 15M seed round. As a physical deep-tech extraction company, Hades publishes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface at this time.

providers.name: Kinder Morgan
providers.description: Kinder Morgan is one of the largest energy infrastructure companies in North America, owning and operating pipelines and terminals that transport natural gas, refined petroleum products, crude oil, carbon dioxide, and other commodities. Kinder Morgan publishes pipeline informational postings and capacity data through Electronic Bulletin Board (EBB) portals; no public REST API or developer program has been identified at this time.

providers.name: NGL Energy Partners
providers.description: NGL Energy Partners LP is a diversified midstream master limited partnership providing transportation, storage, blending, and marketing services for crude oil, natural gas liquids, refined products, and water solutions to producers and end-users across the energy industry. The company is publicly traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol NGL and operates three primary business units: Crude Oil Logistics, Water Solutions, and NGL Liquids.

providers.name: Northvolt
providers.description: Northvolt AB is a Swedish lithium-ion battery developer and manufacturer, founded in Stockholm in 2016, that built and operated the Northvolt Ett gigafactory in Skelleftea and the Northvolt Labs R&D and qualification campus in Vasteras, with further sites in Heide (Germany), Gdansk (Poland) and Montreal (Canada). Its product line covered lithium-ion, sodium-ion and lithium-metal cells, the Voltpack Core and Voltpack Mobile System battery energy storage systems, the Revolt battery recycling operation, and a Connected Battery telemetry and fleet-management service. Northvolt AB filed for bankruptcy in Sweden on 12 March 2025; through 2025 its remaining assets in Sweden, Germany and Poland were acquired by Lyten. The company never published a public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its only named developer-facing surface, api.northvolt.com, no longer has a reachable origin.

providers.name: Calumet
providers.description: Calumet is a specialty hydrocarbon and renewable fuels company that produces a broad portfolio of branded and customer-formulated specialty products including lubricating oils, white mineral oils, solvents, waxes, and renewable diesel through its Montana Renewables subsidiary. The company serves customers across consumer, industrial, and energy markets globally. Calumet does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Chemix
providers.description: Chemix is an artificial-intelligence company building an end-to-end, AI-enabled power system for batteries, organized around the themes of power safety, observability, and predictability. Based in Sunnyvale, California, the company applies generative and machine-learning techniques to make battery behavior more transparent and predictable across the battery lifecycle. Chemix is a Mayfield-backed portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this profile the company is pre-launch ("more product details coming soon") and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this record captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: BrightSource Energy
providers.description: BrightSource Energy is a renewable energy technology company founded in 2006, historically known as a pioneer of utility-scale Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) — it designed, developed and built the 377 MW Ivanpah Solar Electric Generating System in California along with CSP projects in Israel, Dubai and South Africa. In 2022 the company transformed into a software business and now commercializes OASES, a cloud-based, AI-powered Energy Management System (EMS) that forecasts, optimizes and dispatches portfolios of photovoltaics, battery energy storage (BESS), wind, microgrids and EV charging. OASES combines physics-based digital twins, big-data analytics and sensor fusion with an on-site SCADA edge controller ("OASES Gateway + IoT") to run asset management, energy-market bidding and arbitrage, PPA management, grid services and frequency regulation. Engineering is based in Jerusalem, Israel, with a UK office in London. BrightSource does not publish a public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026.

providers.name: Gyre Energy
providers.description: Gyre Energy is a UK-based climate-tech company that reduces cooling costs for operators of cold storage facilities, data centers, and building portfolios by combining artificial intelligence with thermal energy storage. Its platform pairs Gyre AI, a digital twin that learns a facility's thermal behavior and shifts cooling cycles to run when grid energy is cheapest and greenest, with an integrated thermal energy storage "cold battery" and a real-time monitoring and controls layer that tracks temperature, energy use, and door-open events. The company reports up to 50% lower cooling expenses, 38% verified energy cost savings at its first commercial cold storage deployment, a 91% reduction in temperature excursions, and a payback period of under 1.5 years. Gyre Energy is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and, as of July 2026, secured $1.3m in funding to support a major blue-chip deployment and global scaling. It currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Petra Power
