providers.description: Petra Power is an on-site power generation company based in Solon, Ohio, and backed by Techstars, building rapidly deployable, high-efficiency generation systems positioned as "the next 100GW of on-site power." Its technology runs on natural gas, diesel, or hydrogen, claims up to 3x fuel savings versus conventional generators and turbines, and operates silently and odorlessly for use in populated areas. Target applications include data centers, critical backup power, heavy industry, and utility-scale deployment. Petra Power is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Climavision
providers.description: Climavision is a Louisville, Kentucky weather intelligence company that combines a proprietary nationwide supplemental network of low-altitude X-band, dual-polarization gap-filling weather radars with AI-driven numerical weather prediction (NWP) to deliver enterprise-grade forecasts and observational data. Its Horizon AI product line includes Horizon Point for site-specific forecasts, Horizon Global for ground-to-high- altitude global models, Horizon HI-RES for custom high-resolution local forecasting, and Horizon S2S for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction. Climavision exposes a Weather API hosted at point-forecast-api.climavision.com with 1,800+ parameters, 15-day forecasts, and bearer-token authentication, plus a separate Radar Status API and Radar-as-a-Service offering that supplies Level II files, NetCDF, and GeoTIFF radar data products (reflectivity, velocity, dual-pol-derived QPE at 1km, precipitation type, tornado debris detection) for coverage below 4,000 feet where NEXRAD cannot see due to Earth curvature. The company integrates its radar feed into MRMS and has provided supplemental data into the National Weather Service's AWIPS software. Climavision processes 1.5+ billion datasets daily, serves customers across agriculture, aviation, commodity trading, drones and Advanced Air Mobility, energy and utilities, government, insurance and reinsurance, media, and transportation and logistics, and raised a $100 million strategic investment from TPG's Rise Fund. API access is gated through a sales-led contact process; no public sandbox or open-source SDKs are published, and the Climavision GitHub organization (github.com/Climavision) currently has only two minor public repositories (an archived Azure Table Storage helper and a GeoServer Helm chart fork).

providers.name: Liberty Energy
providers.description: Liberty Energy is a North American oilfield services company providing hydraulic fracturing, wireline, sand logistics, and power generation services to onshore exploration and production operators. The company also develops technology solutions for energy completion, ESG reporting, and natural gas fueling. Liberty Energy does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: ProFrac Holding
providers.description: ProFrac Holding Corp. is a vertically integrated, innovation-driven energy services company providing hydraulic fracturing, completion services, and complementary products and services to upstream oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration and production of North American unconventional oil and natural gas resources. The company operates through portfolio brands including ProFrac, Best Pump & Flow, Alpine Silica, IO-TEQ, and Livewire Power. ProFrac Holding does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Riggs Distler
providers.description: Riggs Distler & Company is an energy and utility infrastructure construction firm operating since 1909. Now part of Centuri Group, the company delivers electric transmission and distribution, natural gas, renewable energy, emergency response, and heavy civil services across the United States and Canada. Riggs Distler is a field-services contractor with no public developer APIs or developer portal.

providers.name: Verse Enterprises
providers.description: Verse, Inc. is a San Francisco-based clean energy software company, founded in 2022 and backed by GV (Google Ventures), that helps organizations understand, plan, procure, and operate clean energy portfolios. Its AI-powered platform, Aria, is modular and app-based, turning complex energy, market, and financial data into finance-ready energy intelligence so enterprises can connect to the grid faster, contain electricity costs and risk, and control assets across every market and hour. Verse raised a $20.5M Series A led by GV, with participation from Coatue, CIV, and MCJ Collective, to help organizations reduce electricity costs and emissions.

providers.name: Eneryield
providers.description: Eneryield is a Gothenburg, Sweden based company (a Techstars portfolio company) building AI-powered fault prediction and analytics for electric power systems. Its flagship product, Eneryield IntelliView, uses explainable AI to forecast power outages before they occur by analyzing voltage and current signals from digital relays and merging units on overhead lines, underground cables, and underwater cables. The cloud-based platform integrates directly into existing utility monitoring systems without additional hardware, giving grid operators transparent root-cause analysis so they can move to proactive maintenance and reduce operational cost and downtime. As of this profile, Eneryield publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this record captures its identity and infrastructure posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PowerLight Technologies
providers.description: PowerLight Technologies is an American engineering company headquartered in Kent, Washington that develops laser power beaming systems — wireless transmission of kilowatt-level electrical power over free space and over optical fiber. Founded as LaserMotive and renamed in 2017, the company builds power-over-fiber and free-space laser power links for defense unmanned aerial systems, telecom sites, temporary and disaster power, smart-grid applications, and lunar and satellite power distribution, including work under DARPA's LunA-10 program. Its products are hardware energy-transmission systems rather than software, and the company publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Alpha Natural Resources
providers.description: Alpha Natural Resources is a producer of metallurgical and thermal coal in the United States, mining and processing coal for steelmaking and electric power generation. The company does not offer public developer APIs, but participates in commodity trading data exchanges and supply chain integration with steel producers and utilities.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: NuStar Energy
providers.description: NuStar Energy is one of the largest independent liquids terminal and pipeline operators in the United States, transporting and storing crude oil, refined products, and renewable fuels. NuStar does not currently publish public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: PSEG
providers.description: Public Service Enterprise Group (PSEG) is a diversified energy holding company headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. Its regulated utility subsidiary Public Service Electric and Gas (PSE&G) is New Jersey's largest electric and gas distribution utility, and PSEG Long Island operates the transmission and distribution system on behalf of the Long Island Power Authority. PSEG sits squarely in the utility-retailer tier of the United States energy value chain — it meters, bills, and serves end customers, and it sells generation into the PJM wholesale market rather than publishing that market's data itself. Its API posture is honestly closed. There is no developer portal: developer., developers., api., docs., and data.pseg.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, and /docs on pseg.com return the site's soft-404 page. Green Button is present only as a file: PSEG Long Island's MySmartEnergy FAQ states customers can "download data information in CSV or Green Button (.XML) format," which is Download My Data behind a customer login, not Connect My Data. There is no documented programmatic third-party access to customer usage data — in the New Jersey BPU AMI docket PSE&G described manual secondary-user sharing, a Letter of Authorization with spreadsheets emailed back, and EDI for BPU-licensed suppliers. Grid data is equally closed: the PSE&G NJ and PSEG Long Island outage maps are vendor-hosted KUBRA StormCenter applications with no published data API. Open market data for this territory comes from PJM and the EIA, not from PSEG.

providers.name: Cabot Oil & Gas
providers.description: Cabot Oil & Gas was an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploitation, exploration, production, and marketing of natural gas and oil properties in the United States. In 2021 it merged with Cimarex Energy to form Coterra Energy, which operates across the Permian Basin, Marcellus Shale, and Anadarko Basin.

providers.name: Exxon Mobil
providers.description: Exxon Mobil Corporation is one of the world's largest publicly traded international energy companies, exploring for, producing, and refining oil and natural gas and manufacturing petroleum and chemical products. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Exxon Mobil.

providers.name: TotalEnergies
providers.description: A French multinational integrated energy company operating across oil, natural gas, and low-carbon electricity. One of the largest energy companies in the world with significant investments in solar, wind, and battery storage.

providers.name: AltoTech Global
providers.description: AltoTech Global is a Bangkok-based energy-management technology company building an AI and IoT (AIoT) platform that optimizes energy consumption and reduces carbon emissions across smart buildings. Its Alto CERO air-side and water-side products autonomously tune HVAC, VRF, and chiller-plant systems based on real-time occupancy and conditions, while Alto Digital Twin, Alto Multi-Property, and AltoACE deliver spatial building intelligence, centralized multi-site energy tracking, and AI-assisted facility engineering. Backed by 500 Global, AltoTech serves offices, malls, hotels, banks, and government facilities across Southeast Asia to help accelerate the net-zero economy.

providers.name: Alva Energy
providers.description: Alva Energy is a nuclear technology company rewriting the economics of nuclear deployment to deliver gigawatts of clean power in years, not decades. Rather than building new reactors, Alva productizes capacity upgrades ("uprates") for the existing U.S. reactor fleet: the Alva Uprate combines advanced steam generators with improved heat transfer, a second turbine plant (2TGP) sited outside the protected area, and the DUO-SYNC digital control system, adding roughly 250-300 MWe per reactor as a fixed-price, turnkey project deployable in under two years and targeting 10 GWe across the fleet. The company launched in February 2026 with $33 million in funding led by Playground Global to meet surging power demand from AI and industrial load. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of playground-global and added to the API Evangelist network; Alva Energy publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Astral Systems
providers.description: Astral Systems is a fusion-technology company based in Bristol, United Kingdom, developing Multi-State Fusion (MSF) reactors that produce high-flux neutron sources on demand. Co-founded by Talmon Firestone (CEO) and Dr. Tom Wallace-Smith (CTO), the company applies compact, modular fusion to near-term problems: large-scale medical isotope production to address the global isotope shortage affecting cancer diagnosis and treatment, spent fission fuel analysis, neutronics research, industrial neutron irradiation and accelerated lifetime testing, materials-damage testing, nuclear-waste burnup, and hybrid fission/fusion power. It is a Speedinvest deep-tech portfolio company. Astral Systems is a hardware/deep-tech provider and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Enable Midstream Partners
providers.description: Enable Midstream Partners was a midstream energy company engaged in the gathering, processing, transportation, and storage of natural gas, natural gas liquids, and crude oil. Enable Midstream Partners was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in December 2021 and operations have been integrated into Energy Transfer's midstream business. No public developer APIs are published for this entity.

providers.name: Interface Fluidics
providers.description: Interface Fluidics is a Calgary-based microfluidics company serving the energy industry with high-pressure, high-temperature (HPHT) laboratory testing systems and reservoir fluid analysis services. Its SapphireLab Pro+ platform and standard and custom microfluidic chips deliver direct visual insights for PVT and phase-behavior characterization, enhanced oil recovery (EOR) evaluation, flow assurance studies, and fracturing fluid testing, using small sample volumes at high throughput. Customers include Equinor, ExxonMobil, Chevron, TotalEnergies, and Shell, along with research institutions such as Rice University and PUC-Rio. The company operates customer-facing software (a SapphireLab LIMS portal and desktop apps) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Reflect Orbital
providers.description: Reflect Orbital is a space-technology company developing satellite-based infrastructure to redirect natural sunlight to precise locations on Earth. It offers a Lighting service (adjustable illumination from moonlight to full-daylight intensity, controllable via app or website with no ground infrastructure) and an Energy service (augmenting solar-farm output by directing concentrated sunlight onto photovoltaic arrays). The company plans to expand its constellation from 2 satellites in 2026 toward 50,000+ by 2035. Reflect Orbital is backed by Lux Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, pricing, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: NewMarket Corporation
providers.description: NewMarket Corporation (NYSE: NEU) is a publicly traded specialty chemicals holding company headquartered in Richmond, Virginia. Through subsidiaries Afton Chemical and Ethyl Corporation, NewMarket develops petroleum additives for fuels and lubricants used worldwide.

providers.name: Rizm
providers.description: RIZM is a holistic energy optimization platform for industrial enterprises, operated by Kerith GmbH of Münster, Germany. It integrates data from production, energy procurement, and infrastructure into a digital twin, then optimizes energy system design and day-to-day operational decisions — from long-term infrastructure investment and power purchase agreements to short-term asset dispatch and production scheduling — helping manufacturers cut energy costs and emissions at the same time. Named customers include BMW Group, Bosch, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and BSH. The product is delivered as a login-gated web application (app.rizm.de) with authenticated documentation; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published at this time. Backed by Point Nine, this profile was surfaced from the venture portfolio graph.

providers.name: Skyfri
providers.description: Skyfri is a cleantech software and hardware company headquartered in Oslo, Norway that builds an operating platform for owners and operators of solar and battery energy assets. Founded in 2021, Skyfri combines an edge-native monitoring and control device (the SSI hardware, which speaks Modbus and SCADA over isolated RS-485 ports to inverters, meters, and sensors) with a cloud platform that automates operations, maintenance, and asset performance management. The software delivers real-time data processing, operational management, weather forecasting, dynamic benchmarking, plant insights, and fault detection to monitor generation and address underperformance and equipment failure across a global portfolio of solar and battery assets. The company has offices in Denver, London, Oslo, Singapore, and Bangalore and is backed by Speedinvest. Skyfri exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; its platform is delivered as a customer application at app.skyfri.com.

providers.name: Carnot Innovations
providers.description: Carnot Innovations is a Hong Kong-based building energy management company that applies AI, machine learning, and advanced data analytics to optimize HVAC systems and reduce energy consumption across commercial buildings, data centers, hospitals, railways, and sewage treatment facilities in the Asia-Pacific region. Its platform delivers AI-driven energy optimization, predictive maintenance and fault detection for chillers, pumps, cooling towers, and air handling units, analytics dashboards for facility managers, and continuous commissioning insights, reporting outcomes such as 15% energy cost reductions, 90% hidden-fault detection, and 15 million kWh per year of energy savings across its deployment portfolio. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Carnot Innovations does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: General Electric
providers.description: General Electric Company has reorganized into separate publicly traded companies: GE Aerospace, focused on jet engines and aviation systems, and GE Vernova, focused on energy and power generation. GE HealthCare was spun off in 2023. No unified public developer API portal is currently published by GE Aerospace or GE Vernova.

providers.name: I Flow
providers.description: iFlow Inc. is an energy and water solutions provider headquartered in Santa Ana, California, offering products and services for the sustainable use of vital resources including water metering and leak detection, wastewater management, gas measurement and control, thermal energy/BTU metering, and data connectivity solutions. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Dow
providers.description: Dow Inc. is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow combines science and technology to develop innovative products and solutions for packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications. This entry is an alias of dow-chemical and covers the same parent company.

providers.name: Valar Atomics
providers.description: Valar Atomics is a nuclear energy company developing high-temperature gas reactors (HTGR) with TRISO fuel, graphite moderators, and helium coolant, deployed as grid-independent gigasites of many small reactors that power heavy industry - hydrogen production via the sulfur-iodine cycle, AI data center power, industrial process heat, and clean synthetic hydrocarbon fuels via Fischer-Tropsch synthesis with captured CO2. Its Ward 250 test reactor is a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy, the San Rafael Energy Research Center, and the State of Utah. Founded by Isaiah Taylor and backed by Initialized Capital, the company publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Apollo Atomics Inc
providers.description: Apollo Atomics is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26) nuclear technology company building compact, power-dense pressurized water reactors for electricity generation, industrial process heat, and data-center power. Founded by Assil Halimi and Drew Walker and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company modifies the steam generator of proven pressurized water reactor technology to shrink the plant by roughly an order of magnitude without sacrificing power output, turning a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that can ship on a truck. Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Sense
providers.description: Sense is a Cambridge, Massachusetts energy-intelligence company that builds a residential energy monitor and machine-learning platform for real-time whole-home electricity disaggregation. The Sense Monitor installs in a home electrical panel, samples voltage and current at one million times per second, and uses signature-based machine-learning models to identify individual appliances and loads behind a single point of measurement. The Sense iOS, Android, and web apps surface device-level usage, always-on load, solar production, time-of-use cost, and goal tracking to homeowners. For utilities and grid operators, Sense embeds its disaggregation software into next-generation AMI 2.0 smart meters through partnerships with meter manufacturers such as Landis+Gyr, providing grid-edge visibility, fault detection, load-management, demand-response, and virtual-power-plant enablement. Sense also runs a partner program for smart-device integration with thermostats, EV chargers, heat pumps, and home-service providers. Sense has not released an official public developer API; community developers maintain reverse-engineered, unofficial clients in Python, Node.js, and Home Assistant against an undocumented and unsupported endpoint. Sense's revenue model is hardware sales of the consumer monitor and licensing of its disaggregation software to utilities and meter OEMs.

providers.name: Soma Energy
providers.description: Soma Energy is an AI-powered energy intelligence platform that optimizes how power is produced, stored, and consumed. Founded by former Amazon and technology leaders, it coordinates power generation, battery storage, and large energy consumers such as data centers. Its Intelligence Platform combines three products: AI Trader, which automates energy procurement, hedging, and dispatch for independent power producers (IPPs); BESS Dispatcher, which manages battery energy storage systems; and Load Optimizer, which coordinates data-center workloads with grid conditions to cut energy costs and turn facilities into flexible grid assets. Soma Energy is an early-stage company backed by Uncork Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, developer platform, or documentation.

providers.name: Abaxx
providers.description: Abaxx Technologies is a financial software and market infrastructure company whose principal operating business, Abaxx Exchange, is a centrally-cleared commodity futures and derivatives exchange headquartered in Singapore and focused on energy-transition commodities across four markets: Energy (LNG), Environmental (carbon credits), Battery Materials (nickel, lithium), and Precious Metals. Abaxx Clearing (Abaxx Singapore Clearing Corporation) centrally clears the contracts, and the group also develops SMX (smart data / consensus-formation) technology. Trading runs on the markets.abaxx.exchange platform; market data is distributed to third parties including TradingView (ABAXX: symbol prefix), ipushpull (Microsoft Excel add-in) and LSEG/Refinitiv. Abaxx Technologies is publicly listed (Cboe Canada: ABXX; OTCQX: ABXXF). Abaxx does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI/FIX specification, SDKs or an MCP server; connectivity is arranged through member/broker onboarding. This profile originated as an earlybird portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network and has been enriched with verified public identity and security-posture signals.

providers.name: PECO Energy
providers.description: PECO Energy Company is the largest electric and natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, serving roughly 1.7 million electric and 553,000 natural gas customers across a 2,100-square-mile service territory in southeastern Pennsylvania. Headquartered in Philadelphia and a wholly owned subsidiary of Exelon Corporation, PECO operates a regulated transmission and distribution business that includes a fully deployed smart-meter network, an LNG storage facility in West Conshohocken, and a portfolio of energy-efficiency, demand response, and assistance programs marketed under the Smart Ideas brand. PECO does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose API: its digital surface is delivered through the PECO web portal (peco.com / secure.peco.com), iOS and Android mobile apps, and an internal Exelon Utilities content / configuration API (eudapi.peco.com) that is not documented for third-party use. Customer-authorized programmatic access to interval energy usage is available through the customer-facing My Data / Energy Usage tools and, where supported via the Pennsylvania PUC EDI / data access framework, through third-party data aggregators (UtilityAPI, Arcadia, etc.) using customer credentials.

providers.name: Bidgely
providers.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

providers.name: Enel X
providers.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

providers.name: EnergyBank
providers.description: EnergyBank is a New Zealand deep-tech energy company developing next-generation energy storage for the offshore wind market. Its core approach firms floating offshore wind generation at the turbine so that compute modules can be co-located with the generation itself — taking "data to the power rather than electricity to the data" — which removes the need for a grid connection, enables consentless high-seas deployment, and allows direct ocean cooling of the co-located compute. The company was founded by CEO Tim Hawkey and CTO Alex Szczepaniak, and its team combines applied mathematicians, electronics engineers, and business development staff with advisors drawn from subsea turbomachinery. EnergyBank is venture backed by Version One Ventures, Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, Outset Ventures, Promus Ventures, Nuance Capital, and Boost VC. As of this enrichment pass EnergyBank publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification — it is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API provider.

providers.name: EP Energy
providers.description: EP Energy Corporation was an independent exploration and production company engaged in the acquisition and development of unconventional onshore oil and natural gas properties in the United States. EP Energy filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2019 and emerged in October 2020, with assets later acquired by IKAV in March 2022. The company does not maintain any public APIs, SDKs, or developer resources.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: Kairos Power
providers.description: Kairos Power is an Alameda, California-based advanced nuclear fission company developing the KP-FHR (Kairos Power Fluoride salt-cooled High-temperature Reactor), a Generation IV reactor design that uses TRISO (tri-structural isotropic) fuel pebbles cooled by molten fluoride salt (FLiBe) at low pressure and high temperature. Kairos Power is building Hermes, a low-power demonstration reactor at the East Tennessee Technology Park in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, which became the first non-light-water reactor authorized for construction by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in over 50 years (construction permit issued December 2023). A second unit, Hermes 2, will pair two reactors with a 28 MWe electricity-generating turbine. In October 2024 Google signed a corporate power purchase agreement with Kairos Power for up to 500 MW of nuclear electricity from multiple small modular reactors, with the first deployment targeted by 2030 and additional capacity through 2035 — the first corporate PPA for new advanced nuclear in the United States. The company's revenue model is reactor sales, electricity PPAs, and federal cost-share partnerships (DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program). Kairos Power is privately held, does not expose a public developer API or SDK, and operates under NRC regulatory oversight as a safety-critical nuclear licensee.

providers.name: Modern Electron
providers.description: Modern Electron is a Bothell, Washington energy-hardware company founded in 2015 by Tony Pan (CEO) and Max Mankin (CTO) as a spin-out of Intellectual Ventures. It was built to commercialize advanced thermionic energy converters — solid-state, direct heat-to-electricity devices intended to add on-site generation to combustion and thermal equipment. The company now operates publicly as Modern Hydrogen, applying methane pyrolysis behind the meter to crack natural gas into hydrogen and solid carbon before combustion, for industrial heat and steam, on-site power, data-center energy, asphalt products and heavy-duty fleet fueling. The product is physical equipment installed at customer sites; Modern Electron / Modern Hydrogen operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and its public GitHub organization holds only forks of open-source scientific-computing projects (WarpX, AMReX, PICMI, GPy) used in its own R&D.

providers.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
providers.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy science and energy laboratory. ORNL provides public data and scientific computing resources for research including neutron science, materials science, computing, energy, and national security.

providers.name: Ultra Safe Nuclear
providers.description: Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (USNC) was a Seattle-based advanced nuclear company, founded in 2011, that vertically integrated fourth-generation nuclear power — the Micro Modular Reactor (MMR), the Pylon space reactor developed through its USNC-Tech subsidiary, and Fully Ceramic Microencapsulated (FCM) TRISO nuclear fuel manufactured at Oak Ridge, Tennessee. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in October 2024 following the death of its principal investor, and its assets were sold in a bifurcated Section 363 auction: NANO Nuclear Energy acquired the MMR and Pylon reactor patents and demonstration partnerships for $8.5 million (court-approved 18 December 2024), and Standard Nuclear acquired the FCM/TRISO fuel business and the Oak Ridge facility for $28 million (closed February 2025). The company no longer operates. Its primary domain, usnc.com, is still registered and still routes mail on the Microsoft 365 US Government cloud but publishes no address record, so the corporate web presence is gone. As a reactor and nuclear-fuel manufacturer it never ran a developer program, and no public API, specification, SDK, or agent surface was found under its name.

providers.name: Unigrid
providers.description: UNIGRID Inc. is a San Diego-based sodium-ion battery company founded in 2021 out of UC San Diego Ph.D. research by Dr. Darren H. S. Tan and Dr. Erik A. Wu. Its sodium chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry and alloy anode technology deliver fire-safe, fully passive batteries rated for 30,000+ cycles and -40C to 60C operation, sold as 12V starter batteries (Na+ Fleet), BMS-less rack modules (Na+ Module), residential energy storage (Na+ Casa), and DC rack systems for commercial, industrial, and data center use (Na+ Cleo). Cells are UN38.3 and UL 9540A certified. Backed by Transition VC, Ritz Venture Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Foothill Ventures via an oversubscribed $12M Series A (2024); shipped its first sodium-ion residential batteries in July 2026. UNIGRID publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Calpine
providers.description: Calpine Corporation was a major U.S. energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, and was the largest generator of electricity from natural gas and geothermal energy in the United States. It operated 80 power plants with approximately 26,035 megawatts of generation capacity, including The Geysers, the world's largest geothermal complex. Calpine also operated the Champion Energy retail electricity subsidiary serving deregulated markets. As of January 2026, Constellation Energy completed its acquisition of Calpine for $16.4 billion, making it a business unit of Constellation. Calpine does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Darling Ingredients
providers.description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Elektrik App
providers.description: Elektrik is a medium voltage (MV) equipment procurement platform for electrical distributors, contractors, and Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms. Founded in 2020 by Mario Dealba out of the Techstars Alabama EnergyTech Accelerator, the company streamlines sourcing of medium- to high-voltage supplies (roughly 5kV-35kV / 600V-69kV) including MV cable, terminations, splices, deadbreak and loadbreak connectors, and transformers. Buyers build part lists and specifications in the web app and Elektrik surfaces matching products across leading manufacturers such as TE Connectivity, BURNDY, Richards Manufacturing, and PFISTERER, compressing a traditionally slow, quote-driven procurement cycle. Backed by Techstars and growth capital, Elektrik is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Global Partners LP
providers.description: Global Partners LP is a leading independent owner, supplier, and operator of liquid energy terminals, fueling locations, and retail experiences. The company distributes gasoline, distillates, residual oil, renewable fuels, crude oil, and propane across the Northeast United States through an integrated network of terminals, gas stations, and convenience stores.

providers.name: Holtec International
providers.description: Holtec International is a privately held American supplier of equipment and systems for the nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil power-generation industries. The company is best known for its spent-fuel storage and transport casks (HI-STAR, HI-STORM, HI-STORE CISF), decommissioning services through Holtec Decommissioning International (HDI), and its in-development SMR-300 small modular reactor — a roughly 320 MWe two-loop pressurized water reactor with an 80-year design life. Holtec is currently pursuing the first-ever restart of a permanently shut-down U.S. commercial nuclear power plant at Palisades in Michigan, which is also designated as the first deployment site for the SMR-300. The company runs manufacturing facilities in Camden, NJ, Pittsburgh, PA, and Orrville, OH, and partners with Hyundai Engineering & Construction (HDEC) on SMR-300 detailed design and full-scope plant construction.

providers.name: Inviscid AI
providers.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

providers.name: MDU Resources Group
providers.description: MDU Resources Group is a diversified natural resources company with operations in regulated energy delivery, construction materials, and construction services. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: Moment Energy
providers.description: Moment Energy is a Coquitlam, British Columbia clean-energy company that builds battery energy storage systems (BESS) from repurposed electric-vehicle batteries for commercial and industrial customers. Its Luna BESS is described as the first repurposed-battery system to achieve UL 1973, UL 9540, and UL 9540A certifications, and is applied to demand-charge management, grid backup, EV-charging support, and energy arbitrage across data centers, public institutions, transportation, food & beverage, manufacturing, and forestry. Moment Energy is a hardware and energy-services company and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Phillips 66
providers.description: Phillips 66 is a diversified energy manufacturing and logistics company with midstream, chemicals, refining, and marketing and specialties businesses. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for Phillips 66.

providers.name: Utility Global
providers.description: Utility Global is a Houston, Texas industrial decarbonization company founded in 2018. Its proprietary H2Gen and eXERO platform converts water into high-purity hydrogen using the residual electrochemical energy already present in industrial off-gases and biogenic gases — driving water electrolysis without electricity — while concentrating CO2 into a separate capture-ready stream. The company sells into steel, low-carbon fuels, and refining, petrochemicals and chemicals, and has run demonstration programs on blast-furnace off-gas at commercial steel facilities. It is a hardware and process-technology business, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer program, no API documentation, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: ChampionX
providers.description: ChampionX provides oilfield and gas technology solutions, including chemical technologies, artificial lift systems, digital monitoring platforms, and emissions monitoring equipment. The company serves upstream and midstream operators around the world. ChampionX does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Dresser-Rand Group
providers.description: Dresser-Rand Group was a global supplier of rotating equipment solutions to the worldwide oil, gas, petrochemical, and process industries. It was acquired by Siemens in 2015 and now operates as part of Siemens Energy.

providers.name: First Solar
providers.description: First Solar is a leading global provider of comprehensive photovoltaic (PV) solar energy solutions, designing and manufacturing thin-film solar modules. No public developer portal or open APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: FMC Technologies (now TechnipFMC)
providers.description: FMC Technologies was a Houston-based energy services and equipment company serving the upstream oil and gas industry, particularly subsea, surface, and measurement solutions for hydrocarbon production. In January 2017 FMC Technologies completed its merger with Technip to form TechnipFMC, a global energy services company serving the subsea, surface, and offshore project markets. This repository tracks the legacy FMC Technologies brand and any successor APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with the merged TechnipFMC entity. No public APIs or developer programs are currently published.

providers.name: ICF (ICF International)
providers.description: ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI), formerly ICF International, is a global consulting and digital services firm headquartered in Reston, Virginia, delivering management, technology, and policy consulting to US federal agencies, state and local governments, utilities, and commercial clients. ICF serves markets spanning government, energy, environment, infrastructure, transportation, health, education, social programs, public safety, and disaster management, with approximately 9,000 employees worldwide. The firm has invested in an in-house AI offering branded "ICF Fathom," but no public REST APIs, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation have been identified. ICF's work is delivered under contract rather than through a productized developer platform.

providers.name: Marathon Oil
providers.description: Marathon Oil was an independent international energy company that engaged in the exploration, production, and marketing of liquid hydrocarbons and natural gas. The company was acquired by ConocoPhillips in 2024, and its public web presence now redirects to ConocoPhillips. No public developer APIs have been identified.

providers.name: Newcleo
providers.description: Newcleo is a nuclear energy company founded in September 2021 by Stefano Buono, Luciano Cinotti and Elisabeth Rizzotti, headquartered in Paris with operations across France, Italy, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Belgium and Slovakia. It designs small modular lead-cooled fast reactors (LFR) fuelled with mixed oxide (MOX) fuel made from reprocessed spent nuclear fuel, with the aim of closing the nuclear fuel cycle and reducing long-lived waste. The group employs roughly 1,000 people, has raised over EUR 780 million, and has grown by acquisition (Hydromine Nuclear Energy, SRS-Fucina, Rutschi Group). Newcleo publishes no public developer API or developer program; its only public machine-consumable software is a small set of open-source scientific Python libraries released through its newcleo-dev-team GitHub organisation.

providers.name: Genesis Energy
providers.description: Genesis Energy is a diversified midstream energy master limited partnership with a focus on providing services to refineries, crude oil and natural gas producers, and industrial and commercial enterprises.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: The Nuclear Company
providers.description: The Nuclear Company (TNC) is a U.S.-based nuclear energy infrastructure firm deploying nuclear power at fleet scale with a "design once, build many" standardized construction approach. Through its Powerhouse Resources arm it provides maintenance, outage execution, turbine, electrical, and instrumentation services to nuclear plants nationwide, and its proprietary AI-driven Nuclear Operating System (NOS) manages deployment and operations across the nuclear lifecycle. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company and portfolio company of True Ventures.

providers.name: Adams Resources & Energy
providers.description: Adams Resources & Energy is a diversified energy company engaged in the marketing, transportation, terminalling, and storage of crude oil and other related petroleum products in select markets across the United States. Through its subsidiaries GulfMark Energy, Firebird Bulk Carriers, Phoenix Oil, and Victoria Express Pipeline, the company purchases approximately 90,000 barrels per day at the wellhead and operates over 260 tractor-trailers and 112 pipeline inventory locations. Adams Resources & Energy serves multiple U.S. petroleum basins including the Gulf Coast, Eagle Ford Shale, Permian Basin, Bakken Shale, and Michigan, with over $1 billion in annual revenues and 400+ employees.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Anadarko Petroleum
providers.description: Anadarko Petroleum Corporation was one of the world's largest independent oil and natural gas exploration and production companies, with operations across the United States, the deepwater Gulf of Mexico, and international locations including Mozambique and Ghana. Anadarko was acquired by Occidental Petroleum in August 2019 in a $55 billion transaction. The company was known for its operations in the Wattenberg Gas Field in Colorado, the Delaware Basin in Texas, and major deepwater projects. Anadarko did not offer public developer APIs; its technology integrations were primarily through enterprise systems for partners and joint venture operators.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Blueprint Power
providers.description: Blueprint Power was a New York City software company, founded in 2017 by Robyn Beavers, that turned commercial real estate portfolios into virtual power plants. Its cloud platform connected to distributed energy assets in buildings — solar, batteries, cogeneration — and used data-driven and machine-learning models to aggregate, orchestrate and transact that surplus capacity into wholesale energy markets. It raised a $3.5M Series A (Congruent Ventures, MetaProp, Fifth Wall, Fred Wilson, Brad Burnham) and was acquired by bp in October 2021, joining the bp Launchpad portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public surface: www.blueprintpower.com returns a 301 permanent redirect to bp.com/retailenergy, and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public GitHub organization could be found. Retained in the network as an acquired-company record with no API surface.

providers.name: CDI Corp
providers.description: CDI Corp (CDI Corporation) is a multidisciplinary engineering and technical resourcing firm founded in Philadelphia in 1950 as Comprehensive Designers, Inc., later listed on the NYSE from 1988 to 2017. After being taken private by AE Industrial Partners in September 2017 for approximately $176M ($8.25 per share), AE divested CDI's aerospace business to Belcan (2017), talent and technology services to Artech (2018), and architecture/engineering subsidiary L.R. Kimball to TranSystems (2021), refocusing the remaining CDI Engineering Solutions on integrated engineering, design, project support, procurement, and construction management for the energy and chemicals industries. On January 1, 2025 CDI Engineering Solutions, LLC became a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Consulting Engineers and now trades as Tata Consulting Engineers USA, LLC, headquartered in Houston, TX with 650+ employees across ten engineering centers. CDI Corp has no public developer APIs; the company delivers engineering services and staff augmentation rather than software products. The tagline carried by the operating business is "Quality Results. Sustainable Solutions. Safely Delivered."

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Chesapeake Energy
providers.description: Chesapeake Energy Corporation was an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, focused on unconventional natural gas and oil fields onshore in the United States. In October 2024, Chesapeake combined with Southwestern Energy to form Expand Energy Corporation, which now operates as the largest natural gas producer in the United States. Chesapeake Energy does not currently expose a public developer API; royalty owners and partners interact through the Owner Online Accounts portal, and investors are served via the Expand Energy investor relations site.

providers.name: Chevron
providers.description: Chevron Corporation is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, with operations across upstream exploration and production, downstream refining and marketing, and the production and transportation of crude oil, natural gas, refined fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals, and renewable fuels. Chevron is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and operates globally under brands including Chevron, Texaco, and Caltex. Chevron does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; supplier and partner integrations are handled through the Chevron Invoice and Payment Status (CIPS) system and the Supplier Relations channels, and investors and stakeholders are served through corporate, sustainability, and IR websites.

providers.name: Cimarex Energy
providers.description: Cimarex Energy was an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations focused in the Permian Basin and the Mid-Continent. In October 2021 Cimarex Energy combined with Cabot Oil & Gas Corporation to form Coterra Energy (NYSE: CTRA). No public Cimarex-branded developer APIs exist; all current digital channels and any future API offerings are part of Coterra Energy.

providers.name: Crestwood Equity Partners
providers.description: Crestwood Equity Partners LP was a master limited partnership that owned and operated midstream energy assets across the United States, including natural gas, NGL, and crude oil gathering, processing, storage, and transportation businesses. Crestwood was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in November 2023, with Crestwood common and preferred units ceasing trading on the NYSE on November 3, 2023; ongoing operations and partner contracts have been integrated into Energy Transfer's pipeline and midstream network. Crestwood does not publish a public developer API program; technical interfaces such as nominations, scheduling, and capacity portals are now handled through Energy Transfer's commercial systems.

providers.name: DCP Midstream Partners
providers.description: DCP Midstream Partners is a midstream energy company that gathers, processes, transports, stores, and markets natural gas and natural gas liquids (NGLs) across major U.S. producing regions. Following Phillips 66's acquisition of the remaining public units in 2023, DCP Midstream now operates as part of Phillips 66's midstream segment. The company does not publish a public developer API; integration with shippers and customers is handled through customer portals (tariffs, electronic flow measurement) rather than a self-service API.

providers.name: Dominion Energy
providers.description: Dominion Energy is one of the nation's largest producers and transporters of energy, providing electricity and natural gas to customers across multiple U.S. states including Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, and Utah. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Dominion Resources
providers.description: Dominion Resources is the former name of Dominion Energy, one of the nation's largest producers and transporters of energy, providing electricity and natural gas to customers across multiple U.S. states. The company rebranded from Dominion Resources to Dominion Energy in 2017. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Ecovate
providers.description: Ecovate (Ecovate Energy Indices) is an Israeli energy-data company that operates a platform for the wholesale electricity market price index. It publishes benchmark indices and analytics tracking wholesale electricity market prices, giving energy suppliers, large consumers, traders, and regulators a transparent reference for the cost of electricity in the wholesale market. Ecovate was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The company's public presence is a marketing/product site (Hebrew and English editions) and it does not currently publish a developer program, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Edviro
providers.description: Edviro is an AI platform for building operations and energy optimization, aimed at facility managers and building operators of large commercial buildings. It pulls scattered building data - utility bills, smart meters, building management systems (BMS), submeters, sensors, and work-order platforms - into one place, then follows an Ingest, Detect, Act, and Verify workflow: it consolidates the data, catches energy waste and anomalies in real time, dispatches work orders and adjusts setpoints, and proves the resulting savings against meter data and utility bills. The platform also builds a digital twin of each building to simulate capital projects and forecast ROI before purchase, and produces audit-grade Measurement and Verification (M&V) reporting. Edviro is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Electio
providers.description: Electio (Electio Technologies) is a San Francisco-based, General Catalyst-backed software company building modern control-system software for energy production and transportation infrastructure. The company modernizes the legacy industrial control layers behind power generation, oil and gas, and transportation networks with next-generation software for monitoring, automation, and operational reliability. Electio is an early-stage, largely stealth company: it publishes a company website, a careers page, a contact page, and a privacy policy, but has not released a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile. This entry was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Electroflow
providers.description: Electroflow Technologies is a United States deep-tech company (founded 2023, headquartered in San Bruno, California) developing an electrochemical direct lithium extraction (DLE) process that pulls lithium from dilute North American brines containing under 200ppm lithium using renewable electricity and minimal chemicals. Its cell uses anodes that absorb lithium ions from brine on one pass and release them into a carbonate solution on the reverse pass, producing battery-grade lithium carbonate that is reacted with iron and phosphate to make lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode powder domestically — a three-step route versus the traditional ten-step process, targeting LFP material at roughly 40% below Chinese producers. The company raised a $10M seed round in October 2025 led by Union Square Ventures with Voyager Ventures, Fifty Years, and Harpoon Ventures, and counts Breakthrough Energy among its backers. Electroflow is a hardware and battery-materials company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Eltek
providers.description: Eltek is a Norwegian power-electronics and telecom power-systems manufacturer (DC power rectifiers, industrial and telecom energy systems, the Flatpack product family) now operating as part of Delta Electronics. Its primary domain eltek.com 301-redirects to Delta's standard telecom power solutions catalog (www.delta-emea.com). This is a physical-hardware brand: no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface was found. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub via the sierra-ventures VC pipeline; profile retained for domain-security signal and future re-check.

providers.name: Enbala
providers.description: Enbala Power Networks was a distributed-energy-resource (DER) and grid-flexibility software company (Concerto DER management platform). It was surfaced as an obvious-ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass the company has no live public developer or API presence. enbala.com serves an expired TLS certificate and 301-redirects to www.generacgs.com (Generac Grid Services), which no longer resolves in DNS. No OpenAPI, docs host, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, or webhook surface could be located. Treat this profile as a defunct/acquired lead rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Endurance Energy
providers.description: Endurance Energy is a renewable-energy developer building subsea geothermal power systems that harness volcanic activity beneath the seafloor to generate continuous, weather-independent electricity. Its first product, Adelie, is a planned 100 kW subsea power system slated for deployment in September 2026 at the Axial Seamount caldera off the Oregon coast, targeting island nations, industrial facilities, and data centers that need firm baseload power. The company is venture-backed (a Series A led by Founders Fund) and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Felicis portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public developer surface, API, SDK, or documentation; this entry captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: EnerSys
providers.description: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, manufacturing batteries, chargers, accessories, and outdoor equipment enclosures. EnerSys serves motive power, reserve power, aerospace and defense, and specialty markets. While EnerSys offers a number of customer-facing web tools (Battery Sizing Program, Motive Power configurator, CARB Compliance Calculator) and product-level telemetry such as the Wi-iQ battery monitoring system and NexSys iON connected fleet platform, no public developer APIs or open specifications have been published as of this index.

providers.name: ENGIE Insight Services
providers.description: ENGIE Insight Services (formerly Ecova, now operating as ENGIE Impact) is a sustainability and resource-management company that helps corporations, cities, and governments reduce their environmental footprint and operating costs. It provides energy, water, and waste expense management, utility bill auditing and payment, data management, sustainability consulting, and decarbonization strategy across a large portfolio of client sites. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile has been enriched with domain-security and discovery probes; the company publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Envision Energy
providers.description: Envision Energy is a Chinese green-technology company founded in 2007 by Lei Zhang and headquartered in Shanghai. It designs and manufactures smart wind turbines, operates one of the world's largest fleets of connected wind and solar assets, and builds net-zero industrial parks. Its business spans energy storage and batteries (through Envision AESC), green hydrogen and green ammonia, and the EnOS AIoT operating system delivered by its Envision Digital arm, which connects and manages energy and IoT devices at scale. Envision was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; its public digital surface is a marketing site and the EnOS platform, which is documented on region-restricted hosts not reachable for spec discovery in this pass.

providers.name: EQT Corporation
providers.description: EQT Corporation is the largest producer of natural gas in the United States, headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. EQT operates in the Appalachian Basin and combines exploration and production technology with environmental stewardship initiatives, including a Scope 1 and Scope 2 net-zero commitment. EQT does not maintain a public developer program or open APIs; data access is limited to investor relations, ESG reporting, and partner-facing portals such as Equitrans Midstream customer services.

providers.name: Fourth Power
providers.description: Fourth Power is a grid-scale thermal energy storage company building a "thermal battery" that stores electricity as heat. Surplus wind and solar power is used to heat blocks of graphite to roughly 2,400 degrees Celsius; molten tin, circulated by an all-ceramic pump, moves that heat in and out of storage, and thermophotovoltaic (TPV) cells convert the stored heat back into electricity when the grid needs it. The company positions the system as a cheaper, longer-duration alternative to lithium-ion for firming a clean grid, and operates a megawatt-scale demonstration facility near Boston. Fourth Power raised a Series A led by DCVC in 2023. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fourth Power is a hardware and energy company and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: GlassPoint
providers.description: GlassPoint is an industrial solar process heat company founded in 2009 that designs, builds, owns and operates enclosed-trough solar thermal systems delivering steam to industrial customers under a Steam-as-a-Service model. Its enclosed trough places mirrors inside a glasshouse to cut capital cost and wind loading, and it has delivered commercial solar process steam since the Amal project in Oman went online in 2012, followed by Miraah and the Ma'aden Solar I project in Saudi Arabia. The company sells decarbonized industrial heat and energy plants, not software: it operates a marketing and press site at glasspoint.com and publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Greenchoice
providers.description: Greenchoice is a Dutch energy supplier focused on green electricity and gas, offering renewable energy contracts, solar panels, heat pumps, and EV charging services to consumers and businesses in the Netherlands.

providers.name: Hawaiian Electric Industries
providers.description: Hawaiian Electric Industries (HEI) is a Hawaii-based holding company whose primary subsidiaries provide electric utility service to roughly 95% of Hawaii's residents through Hawaiian Electric, and clean-energy investments through Pacific Current. HEI does not publish public developer APIs at this time; this index tracks the company and its subsidiaries for API discovery purposes.

providers.name: Hess Corporation
providers.description: Hess Corporation was an independent global energy company engaged in the exploration, development, production, transportation, purchase, and sale of crude oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas. Its core operations centered on onshore unconventional production in the Bakken Shale of North Dakota and a major offshore position in the Stabroek Block in Guyana, with additional interests in the Gulf of Mexico, Canada, and Southeast Asia. Chevron Corporation completed its $53 billion all-stock acquisition of Hess on July 18, 2025, after a regulatory and arbitration delay that included a Federal Trade Commission consent order barring former CEO John B. Hess from serving on Chevron's board and a parallel ExxonMobil/CNOOC arbitration over Guyana right-of-first-refusal claims. Hess is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Chevron, and the ONE GUYANA FPSO at Stabroek has come online to produce approximately 250,000 barrels of oil per day. Hess Corporation has never offered public developer APIs; its technology integrations were handled through enterprise partner systems and joint-venture operator portals.

providers.name: HF Sinclair
providers.description: HF Sinclair is an independent energy company that produces and markets gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, specialty lubricant products, and renewable diesel fuel through refineries and a brand network of branded fuel stations.

providers.name: Icahn Enterprises
providers.description: Icahn Enterprises L.P. is a diversified holding company engaged in the investment, energy, automotive, food packaging, real estate, home fashion, and pharmaceutical industries through its operating subsidiaries. The company does not currently publish public developer APIs; investor relations, SEC filings, and corporate communications are provided through its corporate website.

providers.name: IHS
providers.description: IHS was a global information and analytics company providing critical insight to customers across industries including aerospace, defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, and financial services. IHS merged with Markit in 2016 to form IHS Markit, which was subsequently acquired by S&P Global in 2022. The legacy ihs.com domain now redirects to S&P Global. No public IHS-branded APIs are tracked here; current API offerings live within S&P Global product lines.

providers.name: Infocast
