providers.description: Infocast is an event management company (acquired by Clarion Events in 2024) that has produced premier deal-making conferences and summits for more than 35 years across energy, finance, infrastructure, manufacturing, and emerging technology sectors. Infocast does not currently publish a public API.

providers.name: Jinsheng New Energy
providers.description: Guangdong Jinsheng New Energy Co., Ltd. (广东金晟新能源股份有限公司) is a Chinese lithium-battery recycling and materials company headquartered in Zhaoqing, Guangdong, founded in 2010 and originally focused on nickel sulfate production. It operates a closed-loop "urban mine" business: harmless treatment, echelon (second-life) use and hydrometallurgical regeneration of retired lithium-ion batteries into battery-grade nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate, manganese sulfate and lithium carbonate, plus ternary and iron-phosphate precursors and LFP cathode material, and downstream cells for light mobility, commercial and industrial storage, outdoor power stations and solar street lighting. Production is split across Zhaoqing (Gaoyao) in Guangdong and Yichun/Ganzhou in Jiangxi through the wholly owned subsidiary Jiangxi Ruida New Energy Technology, with approved processing capacity of about 204,000 tonnes of spent lithium battery per year. Both the parent and Jiangxi Ruida appear on MIIT's echelon-use and regeneration white lists. The company completed a Series C, is a Hurun and Forbes unicorn-list member, and has pursued a public listing. It is an industrial materials manufacturer and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Lansing Trade Group
providers.description: Lansing Trade Group was an international merchandiser, marketer, and logistics company specializing in bulk commodities including grains, biofuels, and energy products. In 2022, The Andersons completed the acquisition of Lansing Trade Group; its commodities business now operates as part of The Andersons' Trade Group.

providers.name: Liberty Energy
providers.description: Liberty Energy Inc (NYSE: LBRT), formerly Liberty Oilfield Services, is a Denver-based energy services company. It is one of the largest providers of completion services (hydraulic fracturing, wireline, sand and logistics) to onshore oil, natural gas, and enhanced geothermal producers in North America, and it is rapidly pivoting into distributed power generation for data centers and AI infrastructure via its Liberty Power Innovations (LPI) subsidiary. Founded in 2011 by Chris Wright, who left in 2025 to become the 17th US Secretary of Energy under the Trump administration. Ron Gusek is now President and CEO. The company does not publish any public developer APIs; this profile documents the organization, its proprietary internal platforms (FracTrends, Sentinel, digiTechnologies), and the Liberty Power data center pivot.

providers.name: Linear Labs
providers.description: Linear Labs is an industrial motor technology company headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, building high-torque motor systems for wind, nuclear, pumps, actuators, mining, and defense applications. Its patented Hunstable Electric Turbine (HET) permanent-magnet architecture uses a circumferential flux design the company states delivers 2x torque density, 97% peak efficiency, and 50% weight reduction versus conventional motors, scaling from 10 kW to 2.2 MW. Its PitchPro 2000 is a complete pitch-system replacement for aging GE 1.5 wind turbines, pairing the HET motor with KEBA drive electronics, a Bachmann PLC controller, and ultracapacitor backup power. Linear Labs is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable technical surface; this profile is maintained for network coverage and identity only.

providers.name: Marathon Petroleum
providers.description: Marathon Petroleum is one of the largest petroleum product refiners, transporters, and marketers in the United States, with operations including refineries, pipelines, terminals, and retail outlets. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Marianaminerals
providers.description: Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated critical-minerals company supplying the metals essential to modern energy, artificial intelligence, and defense technologies. The company currently develops copper and lithium production projects, with plans spanning cobalt, aluminum, graphite, uranium, and rare earth metals, and is headquartered in San Francisco with an engineering office in Houston. Backed by Khosla Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: MarkWest Energy Partners
providers.description: MarkWest Energy Partners was a master limited partnership engaged in the gathering, processing, and transportation of natural gas and natural gas liquids. The company was acquired by MPLX in 2015 and its operations have since been consolidated under the MPLX brand. No public developer APIs are offered under the MarkWest Energy Partners name.

providers.name: National Oilwell Varco
providers.description: National Oilwell Varco (NOV) is a global provider of equipment, technology, and services for the oil and gas drilling industry. NOV designs and manufactures rigs, drilling tools, downhole equipment, and provides digital solutions for drilling operations worldwide.

providers.name: Nerviom
providers.description: Nerviom is a Y Combinator-backed startup building AI workflows for infrastructure site predevelopment. Its platform deploys AI-assisted workflows tailored to each stage of predevelopment across data centers, energy, manufacturing, telecom, commercial, and mining sites — helping teams surface permitting, zoning, compliance, and interconnection risks earlier, make repeatable execution processes that do not scale linearly with headcount, and consolidate scattered PDFs, portals, and spreadsheets into a single operating view. Nerviom is an early-stage company; it currently publishes a marketing and demo-booking site and does not yet expose a public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: New Jersey Resources
providers.description: New Jersey Resources (NJR) is a Fortune 1000 energy services holding company that provides natural gas distribution through New Jersey Natural Gas, retail energy services, midstream assets, and clean energy investments. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: NextEra Energy
providers.description: NextEra Energy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American energy company and one of the largest electric utility holding companies in the United States. It is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from the wind and sun, and a world leader in battery storage. NextEra Energy operates principally through its two subsidiaries, Florida Power & Light (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources. This repository captures the public-facing digital surface, corporate touchpoints, and any developer or data resources for NextEra Energy. No public REST APIs, developer portal, or machine-readable data feeds have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Niko
providers.description: Niko (Niko Energy) is a Mexican clean-energy company focused on energy efficiency for multi-site enterprises. It designs, installs, and finances commercial and residential solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage, wrapping them in embedded financing options that include cash purchase, 12-month interest-free plans, multi-year subscriptions, and power purchase agreements (PPAs). Its Niko Hub dashboard centralizes energy-portfolio management across locations, Niko Care provides 24/7 monitoring and maintenance, and Niko Insurance covers panel hardware. Backed by fintech venture firm QED Investors, Niko pairs solar deployment with consumption analytics and ESG / consolidated reporting. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found on niko.mx as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: NPco
providers.description: NPco (NP Company) is an AI-native physics-simulation startup building AI-powered simulation for aerospace, defense, and energy engineering. Backed by Partech, it positions itself around accelerating physics simulation with AI. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing site (careers plus a contact@npco.ai address) with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs surfaced. This profile remains a lead in the Industrial, Energy & IoT sector pending any future developer/API surface.

providers.name: Oklo
providers.description: Oklo Inc. is a Santa Clara, California advanced fission company designing and deploying small modular reactors under the Aurora powerhouse brand. The Aurora is a liquid-metal (sodium) cooled, metal-fueled fast reactor derived from the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II (EBR-II) lineage, engineered as a "walk-away safe" passively cooled system that is self-stabilizing and self-controlling under loss-of-coolant and loss-of-shutdown conditions. Oklo's reactors are intended to run on recycled high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel, including legacy EBR-II material, with the company building out three vertically integrated fast-reactor businesses: clean power generation, advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling, and medical radioisotope production. The first commercial Aurora is targeted for operation at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by selection into the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Projects, and the company has completed an NRC Phase 1 pre-application assessment. Oklo went public in May 2024 via merger with AltC Acquisition Corp (a SPAC co-founded by Sam Altman, who serves as chairman) and trades on the NYSE under ticker OKLO. Oklo's commercial posture is utility-scale and industrial — selling power, fuel cycle services, and isotopes to data center operators, defense customers, and industrial offtakers — and the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or open source software.

providers.name: Ola Electric
providers.description: Ola Electric is an Indian electric-vehicle manufacturer building electric scooters (the S1 family), electric motorcycles (the Roadster line), and home energy solutions (Ola Shakti battery systems), all designed and produced in India around its in-house 4680 Bharat Cell and ferrite-motor technology. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a nationwide Hypercharger fast-charging network and Hyperservice center footprint across India. As a consumer EV and energy hardware manufacturer, Ola Electric publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API reference; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Panthalassa
providers.description: Panthalassa is a Portland, Oregon public-benefit corporation founded in 2016 that builds ocean wave-energy "nodes" — a buoyant sphere and central tube that convert deep-water wave motion into electricity in the open ocean. Rather than transmitting power to shore, the company pairs each node with sealed, seawater-cooled compute containers so the electrons power AI and data-center workloads at sea, backhauled over satellite link. It has run the Ocean-2 Pacific pilot and markets no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract; this profile records that absence and the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Par Pacific Holdings
providers.description: Par Pacific Holdings is an entrepreneurial liquid fuels company focused on owning and operating energy and infrastructure businesses in logistically- complex markets. The company operates refining, retail, and logistics businesses across Hawaii, Washington, Wyoming, and Montana, with retail brands including 76, Hele, and nomnom.

providers.name: PBF Energy
providers.description: PBF Energy is one of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oils, lubricants, petrochemical feedstocks, and other petroleum products in the United States, operating refineries and a logistics network across the country.

providers.name: Plains GP Holdings
providers.description: Plains GP Holdings owns an interest in Plains All American Pipeline, a publicly traded master limited partnership that owns and operates midstream energy infrastructure in the United States and Canada. No public developer API or developer portal has been published; this repository tracks corporate and investor resources.

providers.name: PowerTap Hydrogen
providers.description: PowerTap Hydrogen Fueling Corp. is an Aliso Viejo, California hydrogen fueling technology company founded in 2020 and operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of the publicly traded PowerTap Hydrogen Capital Corp. (NEO: MOVE, OTC: MOTNF, FWB: 2K6B). PowerTap designs and deploys distributed, on-site "blue hydrogen" production and dispensing stations built on a patented small-scale steam methane reforming (SMR) platform with embedded carbon capture, converting natural gas and municipal water into high-purity hydrogen at the point of use rather than trucking it in. The modular station design is marketed as deployable in weeks instead of months, and the company positions it for heavy-duty trucking and light-vehicle refueling as well as baseload power for data centers. PowerTap technology-based stations operate at private enterprise sites and at a public station near LAX, with additional deployments cited in California, Texas, Massachusetts and Maryland. The company publishes no developer program, no API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; it is profiled here as an energy-infrastructure company, not an API provider.

providers.name: PPL
providers.description: PPL Corporation is a U.S. energy company that delivers electricity and natural gas to customers through its regulated utilities in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, and Rhode Island. PPL is a Fortune 500 company.

providers.name: Praxair
providers.description: Praxair was an American multinational industrial gases company that merged with Linde AG in 2018 to form Linde plc. Praxair operations in the United States now operate as Linde. The company supplies atmospheric, process, and specialty gases, along with related equipment and services to a range of industries.

providers.name: ProPetro Holding
providers.description: ProPetro Holding Corp (NYSE: PUMP) is a Midland, Texas-based oilfield services company that "provides hydraulic fracturing and other complementary services to leading upstream oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration and production of North American unconventional oil and natural gas resources," operating principally in the Permian Basin. Service lines include hydraulic fracturing, the FORCE electric fleet (eFleet), Silvertip Wireline, cementing, PROPWR power solutions, and Aqua Prop water management. ProPetro does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or technology developer portal.

providers.name: Public Service Enterprise Group
providers.description: Public Service Enterprise Group (PSEG) is a publicly traded diversified energy holding company headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. Through its subsidiaries including PSE&G and PSEG Power, the company provides regulated electric and natural gas distribution and operates electric power generation across the northeastern United States. PSEG is a Fortune 500 company. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Pulse Space
providers.description: Pulse (Pulse - Space Power Solutions) is a Techstars-backed space technology company building power solutions for spacecraft and satellites. The company operates a WebGL marketing site at pulsespace.com and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment probing confirmed a marketing-only web presence (TLS 1.3 with HSTS) and no developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Quanta Services
providers.description: Quanta Services is a Fortune 500 specialty contracting company that delivers infrastructure solutions to the electric power, renewable energy, oil and gas, pipeline, and communications industries throughout North America and Australia.

providers.name: Radiant
providers.description: Radiant is a nuclear technology company developing portable, transportable microreactors designed to deliver clean, reliable power to remote sites, military installations, disaster-relief operations, and industrial locations that today depend on diesel generators. Its flagship Kaleidos reactor is a factory-built, containerized ~1 MW microreactor intended to ship by truck, plane, or ship and be operational quickly on-site. Founded by former SpaceX engineers and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Radiant is backed by DCVC and Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Resilient Power Systems
providers.description: Resilient Power Systems is a power-electronics hardware company known for solid-state and medium-voltage power distribution and conversion systems, including solid-state transformers for grid, EV fast-charging, and industrial applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass its web presence (resilientpower.com) has moved and now redirects to Eaton, following acquisition; the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other API-consumable surface, so this profile is identity-only. Enrichment probes confirmed the redirect and captured live domain-security posture for the remaining host.

providers.name: Salient Energy
providers.description: Salient Energy is a Dartmouth, Nova Scotia based clean-energy hardware company developing zinc-ion batteries as a safer, lower-cost alternative to lithium-ion for renewable energy storage and grid applications. Its cells use a non-toxic, water-based electrolyte that eliminates fire risk, and are built from low-cost zinc and manganese materials sourced in North America, with a roughly 50% lower production carbon footprint than lithium-ion. The company positions its technology as a scalable answer to lithium supply constraints for stationary energy storage. Salient Energy manufactures physical battery hardware and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Seventy Seven Energy
providers.description: Seventy Seven Energy Inc. was a diversified oilfield services company headquartered in Oklahoma City, providing wellsite services and equipment to U.S. land-based oil and natural gas exploration and production customers. It was formed in 2011 out of Chesapeake Energy's oilfield services arm and spun off as an independent public company, operating through affiliates including Nomac Drilling (contract land drilling), Performance Technologies (hydraulic fracturing and pressure pumping) and Great Plains Oilfield Rental (rental tools and equipment). After the 2014-2016 oil price collapse it completed a prepackaged Chapter 11 restructuring and recapitalization, emerging in August 2016. THE COMPANY NO LONGER EXISTS. Patterson-UTI Energy completed its merger with Seventy Seven Energy on 20 April 2017 in a transaction valued at roughly USD 1.76 billion, issuing about 47.5 million shares and repaying USD 472 million of Seventy Seven Energy debt at closing; Nomac was absorbed into Patterson-UTI Drilling and Performance Technologies into Universal Pressure Pumping. Seventy Seven Energy never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and there is no surviving entity to publish one — its own domain, seventysevenenergy.com, no longer resolves.

providers.name: Solactron
providers.description: Solactron, Inc. is a Silicon Valley solar technology company developing high-performance, monolithically integrated thin-film solar modules on glass substrates. Its proprietary "Thin Film 2.0" process uses a tunable compound chemistry targeting greater than 34% efficiency by capturing over 95% of the solar spectrum, aiming for the highest efficiency and lowest cost at gigawatt scale. Backed by 500 Global, Solactron is a deep-tech hardware and materials manufacturer positioned in the renewable energy and utility-scale photovoltaic market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only (Home, Technology, Company, Careers, Contact) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: SolarBridge Technologies
providers.description: SolarBridge Technologies was a solar power-electronics company that developed AC photovoltaic (ACPV) technology for residential and commercial solar, including its TrueAC modules, the Pantheon and Pantheon II microinverters, and the SolarBridge Management System for monitoring installed systems. The company was acquired by SunPower in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent business; its former marketing site is preserved at solarbridgetech.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. SolarBridge was a hardware and embedded-electronics company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Solstice
providers.description: Solstice is a community solar platform that lets households, renters, and businesses benefit from renewable energy without installing rooftop panels. Subscribers reserve a portion of a nearby solar farm and earn monthly savings on their electric bill through solar credits, while businesses can purchase community solar subscriptions and renewable energy credits (RECs). Solstice also offers subscriber-management solutions for solar developers and asset owners. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SparkCharge
providers.description: SparkCharge operates one of the world's largest off-grid and mobile EV charging networks, delivering on-demand electric vehicle charging to commercial and fleet operators without fixed grid infrastructure. Its offerings span mobile battery-based charging dispatched by technicians, portable off-grid power hubs, and permanent charging installations, serving delivery, rideshare, automotive, ports, and event customers. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Spectra Energy
providers.description: Spectra Energy was a Fortune 500 American energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, focused on natural gas transmission and storage, distribution, and gathering and processing. Founded in 2007 as a spin-off from Duke Energy, Spectra Energy operated the Texas Eastern Pipeline and other major North American natural gas infrastructure. In February 2017, Spectra Energy was acquired by Enbridge Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $28 billion and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: Spruce Finance *
providers.description: Spruce Power operates sprucepower.com as a customer portal ("CustomerPortal") for its residential solar and home energy services, giving homeowners a dashboard to monitor their solar energy systems and production, manage their service agreement, and get in touch with support (public routes include /dashboard, /monitoring, /pro, and /get-in-touch). Surfaced as a GV portfolio company (sector: frontier-tech) and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or working /.well-known/ discovery surface — all /.well-known/ paths return the customer-portal single-page-app shell rather than real documents, and no api./developer./docs. host resolves.

providers.name: Superior Energy Services
providers.description: Superior Energy Services is a leading provider of specialized oilfield services and equipment for oil and gas exploration, production, and well services. The company operates a portfolio of global brands providing drilling equipment rentals, completion tools, well intervention, and production services across 47 countries. Superior leverages digital transformation technologies including SAP, Azure, and field data platforms to deliver integrated wellbore technology and wellsite solutions.

providers.name: Terranox AI
providers.description: Terranox AI is the first vertically integrated, AI-powered uranium discovery company, founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch. The company finds high-grade uranium deposits in North America by training machine learning models on more than seventy years of exploration outcomes locked in thousands of legacy PDFs, drill logs, and hand-drawn geological maps. Traditional uranium exploration has a hit rate below one percent and timelines measured in decades; Terranox aims to raise that hit rate and compress discovery time to help supply the fuel a global nuclear-energy resurgence needs — the world must roughly quadruple uranium production by 2050. Terranox is a private operating company focused on geoscience and mineral exploration and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. It is backed by General Catalyst, 776 Ventures, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Tibo Energy
providers.description: Tibo Energy is an Eindhoven-based energy software company building an AI-driven Energy Management System (EMS) for commercial and industrial customers. Its SaaS platform simulates, monitors, and autonomously controls on-site energy hubs and smart grids, coordinating distributed assets such as heat pumps, EV charging stations, and battery storage to cut energy costs and emissions and to unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure without waiting for grid upgrades. Tibo connects hardware through standard protocols such as MODBUS and OCPP via the Tibo Gateway and exchanges data with BMS, SCADA, and ERP systems through open APIs. Since launching in late 2023 it has deployed its EMS across more than 30 industrial sites and is backed by KOMPAS VC, Hitachi Ventures, SET Ventures, WEPA Ventures, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Ubiquitous Energy
providers.description: Ubiquitous Energy is a Redwood City, California materials-science company and MIT spin-out that develops UE Power (formerly ClearView Power), a transparent photovoltaic coating applied to glass. The coating uses small-molecule organic semiconductor dyes to absorb ultraviolet and infrared light while transmitting visible light, so a window generates electricity without a visible aesthetic change and while retaining low-e thermal performance. The company designs, synthesizes and characterizes novel organic semiconductor molecules, evaluates transparent photovoltaic devices against industry test protocols, and sells technical consultation, R&D, design and engineering services to glass and glass-coating manufacturers. Its product is a physical coating and a licensing/engineering practice, not software; it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: UGI Corporation
providers.description: UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a King of Prussia, Pennsylvania-based natural gas and electric utility and propane distribution company. UGI Utilities serves Pennsylvania natural gas and electric customers, AmeriGas is the largest retail propane distributor in the United States, and UGI International markets LPG across Europe through brands including Antargaz, Flaga, and AvantiGas. The corporation also operates midstream and energy marketing businesses. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specs, or third-party developer APIs have been identified. Customer self-service runs on a Smart Energy Water (SEW)-powered Online Account Center (Android package com.sew.ugi) with CheckFree Pay handling bill payments; AmeriGas operates the separate MyAmeriGas portal at myamerigas.com. Large commercial customers use an Oracle APEX-based TCP platform at apex.ugi.com. UGI Utilities is not listed as a supported utility by UtilityAPI or other Green Button aggregators at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Wi Charge
providers.description: Wi-Charge is a long-range wireless power company that transmits electricity over the air using infrared light, delivering safe, automatic charging to smart devices from thirty or more feet away without cables, batteries, or charging pads. The company sells consumer products such as the Encode Wireless Power Kit for smart locks and licenses its transmitter platform and compact receiver modules to OEMs building smart-home, commercial, IoT, retail, and consumer-electronics devices. Wi-Charge is venture-backed, including by Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Wi-Charge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a hardware and OEM-licensing business rather than an API-first provider.

providers.name: yinglisolar
providers.description: Yingli Energy Development Co., Ltd. (Yingli Solar) is one of the earliest companies in China to commit to the photovoltaic industry, operating as an integrated photovoltaic smart-energy solution provider spanning technology research and development, smart manufacturing of high-efficiency solar PV modules (PANDA 3.0 and YLM 3.0 series), and the development, construction, and operation of power stations for residential, commercial, and utility-scale applications. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a solar-hardware manufacturer, Yingli publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only online service surfaces are a product anti-counterfeiting verification tool and product-specification downloads.

providers.name: ylhyoil

providers.name: Zap Energy
providers.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. Zap Energy has no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release; the technical surface is published as peer-reviewed papers and DOE milestone reports.

providers.description: Cowboy Clean Fuels (CCF) is a Denver, Colorado climate-technology company, founded in 2020 and operating in Gillette, Wyoming, that produces carbon-negative renewable natural gas (RNG) while permanently sequestering atmospheric carbon dioxide. CCF injects non-food-grade organic biomass — residue products of sugar-beet refining such as molasses — into depleted coal bed methane (CBM) wells in the Powder River Basin, where naturally occurring methanogenic microorganisms convert the feedstock into methane and carbon dioxide; the coal seam then selectively adsorbs and permanently stores the CO2. Its lead development is the Triangle Unit Renewable Energy and Carbon Capture and Storage Project (TRECCS) near Gillette, Wyoming, and in May 2025 it signed an offtake agreement with Mercuria for RNG produced under its BiCRS+RNG methodology. Cowboy Clean Fuels is an energy and carbon-dioxide-removal operator, not a software vendor: it sells molecules and carbon removal credits, and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: Fervo Energy
providers.description: Fervo Energy is a next-generation geothermal power company headquartered in Houston, Texas, that generates carbon-free, always-on electricity through enhanced geothermal systems (EGS). Founded in 2017 by Tim Latimer and Jack Norbeck, Fervo adapts horizontal drilling, distributed fiber-optic sensing, and advanced subsurface data analytics from the oil and gas industry to make geothermal energy viable in previously uneconomic locations. Its projects include the Project Red pilot in Nevada and the flagship 500 MW Cape Station development in Beaver County, Utah. Fervo trades on Nasdaq under the ticker FRVO and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network surfaced from the DCVC portfolio; Fervo Energy is a physical energy-infrastructure company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: FirstFuel Software
providers.description: FirstFuel Software was a business-focused energy analytics SaaS company that used utility meter and building data to profile commercial and industrial customers, helping utilities target energy-efficiency and customer-engagement programs. The company was acquired by Uplight, and the firstfuel.com domain now redirects to uplight.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no active first-party developer surface (no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve, and no OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published), so this profile remains an identity-only record for a company that no longer operates a standalone API program.

providers.name: GridBank
providers.description: GridBank is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: energy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: In Charge One, Inc.
providers.description: In Charge One, Inc. is a hardware startup behind "Socket to Pocket," a paid charging system for electronic devices in public spaces. The device lets visitors charge smartphones, laptops, drones, e-bikes, and scooters at cafes, shops, clinics, stadiums, airports, and other venues by tapping a card and paying for access, while venue owners monetize the outlet and earn a commission per plugged socket. It ships in wall-mounted, extension-cord, and anti-vandal street versions. Founded in 2023 by Danylo (Daniel) Tonkopii, co-founder of Delfast electric bikes, and Andriy Zinchuk, the company is based in Los Angeles, California and was developed by Ukrainian engineers. It is a consumer/commercial hardware and payments business, not an API provider: no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published, and its incharge.one domain is currently non-resolving and in registrar redemption/pending-delete status. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is retained as an identity record.

providers.name: Magellan Midstream Partners
providers.description: Magellan Midstream Partners owned the longest refined petroleum products pipeline system in the United States, along with refined petroleum products and crude oil storage facilities. Magellan Midstream Partners was acquired by ONEOK in September 2023 and its assets and operations have been integrated into ONEOK's Refined Products and Crude segment. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts made publicly available related to the legacy Magellan operations or successor ONEOK resources.

providers.name: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power)
providers.description: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power, 慕帆动力) is a Chinese industrial power-equipment manufacturer developing next-generation zero-carbon clean power-generation technology and products. Its portfolio centers on hydrogen-fuelled gas turbine generating sets, high-speed multi-stage cantilever turbines, special-gas and TRT flow-path (通流) turbines, dry low-NOx combustors, and industrial waste-heat and waste-pressure recovery equipment. The company runs a corporate brochure website in Chinese and English (ICP 沪ICP备17001438号) and publishes no public developer, API, or SDK surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northern Tier Energy
providers.description: Northern Tier Energy was an independent downstream energy company with refining, retail, and pipeline operations. It was acquired by Western Refining in 2016, which itself merged into Marathon Petroleum's brand portfolio. No active public APIs are associated with this entity; the repository is maintained as a historical record within the API Evangelist Network.

providers.name: QEP Resources
providers.description: QEP Resources was an independent natural gas and crude oil exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations in the United States. The company was acquired by Diamondback Energy in 2021 and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: Renewable Energy Group
providers.description: Renewable Energy Group (REG) is a North American producer of biodiesel and renewable diesel, founded with biodiesel operations dating to 1996 and formally established as a separate company in 2006, with headquarters in Ames, Iowa. REG operated as a publicly traded company on Nasdaq under the ticker REGI until February 28, 2022, when Chevron Corporation announced the acquisition of REG for approximately $3.15 billion; the deal closed on June 13, 2022, and REG now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Chevron under the Chevron Renewable Energy Group brand at chevron-reg.com. REG operates a fleet of biorefineries across the United States and Europe, producing biodiesel, renewable diesel, and related lower-carbon fuel products from a diversified mix of feedstocks including used cooking oil, inedible animal fats, distillers corn oil, and vegetable oils. As of this profile, neither REG nor the Chevron Renewable Energy Group subsidiary publishes a public consumer-facing developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or GitHub organization; customer, supplier, distributor, and feedstock-partner integrations are handled through Chevron Renewable Energy Group sales, supply, and supplier-relations channels.

providers.name: Rens Energy
providers.description: Rens Energy is a Shanghai-based distributed energy-storage and energy-management company founded in 2017. It builds distributed energy-storage systems and energy-management software that let customers deliver power and energy-balance scheduling, energy-usage analysis, and energy optimization for efficient operation and asset appreciation of their power assets. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment probing found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Sila
providers.description: Sila Nanotechnologies (silanano.com) is a battery materials company that develops and manufactures Titan Silicon, a next-generation silicon anode that replaces graphite in lithium-ion batteries to increase energy density and enable fast charging. Sila operates silicon anode manufacturing facilities and also offers battery engineering services, targeting electric vehicles, consumer electronics, aerospace, data centers, robotics, and defense. The enrichment pass found no developer API, API documentation, or developer portal: Sila is a B2B advanced-materials hardware company with no public API surface.

providers.name: Silver Spring Networks *
providers.description: Silver Spring Networks was a smart-grid, smart-city, and IoT networking company that built wireless canopy networks and the SLV/Data Platform for utilities, offering RESTful Data Platform APIs (device registration, device metadata, sensor data, and webhook event notifications) plus an SDK on its developer portal at developer.ssni.com. Itron completed its acquisition of the company in January 2018 for approximately USD 830 million and rebranded it Itron Networked Solutions; the standalone ssni.com and developer.ssni.com properties are now offline. Enrichment pass 2026-07-21 found no live API surface: all legacy domains fail to resolve and the historical developer portal is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Solar City
providers.description: SolarCity was a San Mateo, California based provider of residential and commercial solar energy systems, founded in 2006 by brothers Peter and Lyndon Rive with backing and board chairmanship from their cousin Elon Musk. The company designed, financed, installed, and monitored rooftop solar and energy-storage systems, and became the largest residential solar installer in the United States before its 2012 IPO (NASDAQ: SCTY). In November 2016 SolarCity was acquired by Tesla, Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at roughly 2.6 billion US dollars and was absorbed into Tesla's energy-generation and storage business; the SolarCity brand was subsequently retired and its products relaunched under Tesla (Solar Roof, Solar Panels, Powerwall). SolarCity no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI surface. The solarcity.com domain remains registered under Tesla's DNS infrastructure but no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Terra AI
providers.description: Terra AI is a geoscience frontier company building specialized artificial intelligence for the natural resources sector, focused on subsurface characterization and exploration optimization for mining and reservoir operators. Its platform integrates exploration data to generate large populations of geological models, helping teams decide where to drill, characterize deposits, and assess project economics earlier — the company cites 50-60% fewer drilling meters and 2-3x more precise resource estimates versus conventional methods. Terra AI raised a $20M Series A led by Khosla Ventures with BHP Ventures in June 2026 and serves copper, gold, rare-earth (REE), and reservoir projects. The company operates on a B2B model and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: VLTA
providers.description: VLTA (Volta Charging) is an electric-vehicle charging network that pairs public EV chargers with digital out-of-home advertising displays at retail, grocery, and shopping destinations. The Volta business was acquired by Shell in 2023; its voltacharging.com domain now redirects to Shell's mobility/EV-charging pages, and consumer charging operations are presented under the JOLT brand (joltcharge.com) offering a mobile app to locate chargers, start/stop sessions, and view pricing. No public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or GitHub organization was found during enrichment; this remains an identity/company profile with no API surface.

providers.name: Talen Energy
providers.description: Talen Energy is an independent power producer and energy infrastructure company and a Fortune 1000 firm. The company operates a portfolio of nuclear, natural gas, oil, and renewable power generation facilities across the United States and supplies wholesale electricity into competitive markets. Talen Energy does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Fulcrum BioEnergy
providers.description: Fulcrum BioEnergy, Inc. was a Pleasanton, California waste-to-fuels project developer founded in 2007 that converted municipal solid waste into synthetic crude oil for refining into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and diesel, using a shred-and-sort feedstock line feeding a gasifier and a Fischer-Tropsch conversion train. Its first and only commercial plant, the Sierra BioFuels Plant in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center outside Reno, Nevada, was designed to take roughly 175,000-219,000 tons of household garbage a year from an adjacent feedstock processing facility and began production in late 2022. The company raised on the order of a billion dollars in equity, debt and government support over its life, including strategic investments and offtake alliances with United Airlines, Waste Management, Cathay Pacific Airways, Marubeni and bp, plus a US Department of Energy loan guarantee, USDA loan guarantee and Department of Defense grants; E. James Macias led it as president and CEO through its build-out years, and it had announced follow-on projects including a Gary, Indiana plant and the NorthPoint facility in the UK. The Sierra plant stopped operating in mid-May 2024 after persistent equipment problems, the company laid off essentially its entire workforce and took its website down, and on 2024-09-09 Fulcrum BioEnergy, Fulcrum Sierra Holdings and Fulcrum Sierra Finance Co. filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware listing more than $456 million owed to over 200 creditors. A November 2024 auction sold the biorefinery to Switch, Ltd. for $55 million and the adjacent feedstock processing facility to Refuse Inc., a WM subsidiary; the plan of liquidation was confirmed in April 2025 and went effective in May 2025. Fulcrum was an industrial energy project developer rather than a software company and never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification — a Wayback index of its corporate site from 2008 through 2024 turns up no developer, reference, or spec path of any kind. Its corporate host fulcrum-bioenergy.com no longer resolves to any web server, and the alternate registration fulcrumbioenergy.com is parked on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Matador Resources
providers.description: Matador Resources Company is an independent energy company engaged in the exploration, development, production, and acquisition of oil and natural gas resources in the United States. The company's operations are primarily focused on the Wolfcamp and Bone Spring plays in the Delaware Basin in Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Matador also operates midstream assets through its San Mateo Midstream subsidiary.

providers.name: Newfield Exploration
providers.description: Newfield Exploration was an independent crude oil and natural gas exploration and production company before being acquired by Encana (now Ovintiv) in 2019.

providers.name: Radiantnuclear
providers.description: Radiantnuclear is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Energy Future Holdings
providers.description: Energy Future Holdings was a Dallas-based privately held energy company involved in electricity generation, mining, wholesale energy trading, transmission and distribution, and retail electricity through subsidiaries Luminant, Oncor, and TXU Energy. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2014 and was succeeded by Vistra Corp (which absorbed Luminant and TXU Energy generation/retail operations) and Sempra Texas Utilities (which acquired Oncor). No active developer APIs are offered under the Energy Future Holdings name.

providers.name: Murphy Oil
providers.description: Murphy Oil is an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company with operations focused in the United States, Canada, and other international locations.

providers.name: Noble Energy
providers.description: Noble Energy was an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company with operations in the United States and several international locations before being acquired by Chevron in 2020.

providers.name: Pioneer Natural Resources
providers.description: Pioneer Natural Resources was a large independent oil and gas exploration and production company with operations focused in the Permian Basin of Texas before being acquired by ExxonMobil. No public APIs or developer resources were published; this entry tracks the company as a non-API operator within the energy sector.

providers.name: Simple Energy
providers.description: Simple Energy was a portfolio company of Techstars, surfaced and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07 enrichment pass, its domain simpleenergy.com no longer hosts a product site; it returns a static page stating the domain is owned by Uplight and immediately redirects to uplight.com. Probing found no public API surface for Simple Energy - no api/developer/docs subdomains resolve, no .well-known endpoints, no OpenAPI, no llms.txt - so this remains an identity-only company record.

providers.name: OGE Energy
providers.description: OGE Energy is the parent company of Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company, a regulated electric utility serving customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas.

providers.name: Oil States International
providers.description: Oil States International is a global oilfield services company that provides specialty products and services to oil and gas drilling and production companies throughout the world.
